- Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:663-671` (marker matcher);
  `verilator/src/hybrid/csr_trigger.hpp` (now matches the same HINTs).
- Status: RESOLVED by the trigger redesign.

### L13. [RESOLVED: exact by construction for SLTI] marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18)

- The matcher still skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes, but

### L14. The SimPoint cycle estimate is an approximation, not a measurement

- When it bites: any `--mode simpoint` / `./hsim.py estimate` run where you
  read the headline `estimated_cycles` as if it were exact.
- What happens: each phase CPI is sampled from a single window of
  `vsim_icount` instructions at the slice boundary (`hsim.py:1126-1225`,
  `_run_simpoint_pipeline`), and the whole-program figure is
  `N_total * weighted_CPI`. Two accuracy gaps:
  1. The microarchitectural state (caches, branch predictor) is cold at
     each window start unless you pass `--vsim-warmup-icount`. Without
     warmup the CPI is biased high.
  2. No error bound or confidence interval is reported. The estimate
     inherits SimPoint's usual phase-approximation error.
- Where: `hsim.py:1126-1225` (`_run_simpoint_pipeline`). Note: SimPoint
  still runs only on the Python golden (`./hsim.py`); the C++ port has not
  landed.
- Status: by design; mitigate with `--vsim-warmup-icount`.

### L21. Andes vendor CSRs are only partially transported  (new 2026-05-28; cache/misc pair landed 2026-06-16)

  micm_cfg, mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec, mslideleg`, ...).
- What happens: the cache machine-setup pair `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA) and
  `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) now round-trips. crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches via
  `csrw mcache_ctl`, but that write runs on the cache-less functional
  engine; without carrying it the cycle engine resumed at the ROI with
  caches at their reset default -- DISABLED -- so the whole window ran
  uncached and the figure was inflated severalfold (hello `main`->`_exit`:
  14707 -> 2871 cycles). All OTHER Andes vendor CSRs still do not appear
  in `hybrid_state_v1`; vsim runs the ROI with whatever its reset /
  boot-time values were, so remaining prefetcher / branch-predictor / ECC
  controls can still shape the cycle count -- an accuracy hazard for those.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl fields, rest
  absent); `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (drains the pair by gdbstub
  name); `resume_driver.hpp` (tolerant restore, `kCsrMcacheCtl` /

- Status: PARTIAL. The cycle-shaping cache pair is transported (the L20
  fix recipe: one `uint64` each carved from `reserved[]`, drained by name,
  restored via abstract-or-PB, no version bump). The remaining vendor CSRs

  boot-set) or software-visible (must round-trip).

### L26. [RESOLVED 2026-06-16] V transport scratch moved above the program's RAM  (new 2026-06-15)

- **Was**: the V-register transport staged 32 vector registers through a fixed
  guest address `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` (15 MiB), INSIDE the program's RAM.
  On every resume on a V-capable core -- the V flag is set from register
  ADVERTISEMENT, not use, so even a program that issues no V instruction
  triggers it -- `ResumeDriver` wrote the drained V bytes there, silently
  clobbering any program data at that address. Repro: `break_vscratch.S`.
- **Why a scratch page is needed at all**: the RISC-V Debug Module has no
  abstract command for `v0..v31`, so vsim moves them by executing `vle8.v` /
  `vse8.v` in the Program Buffer against a known guest-RAM staging page
  (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `program_buffer.hpp`).
- **Fix (scheme D; F1+F2+F3, see `docs/archive/vscratch_reservation.md`)**:
  1. The scratch is no longer a constant -- it is the TOP page of the mapped
     RAM span, `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size) = ram_base + ram_size -
     HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`. ResumeDriver/StateDrain take it as a required-
     when-V argument; a V handoff with it unset throws (no silent transport
     through a bogus address).
  2. The driver maps ONE PAGE MORE than `--mem-size` (`shm.cpp`
     `physical_mmap_bytes`), so the scratch sits at `ram_base + --mem-size` --
     just ABOVE the program's declared RAM. No program layout (low stack,
     top-of-RAM stack, or a heap grown to the ceiling) can reach a page past its
     own RAM, so the scratch can never be clobbered. `--mem-size` is capped at
     2 GiB minus the page.
  3. A load-time guard (`elf_load_top` + `cmd_run.cpp`) rejects an ELF whose
     static image extends into the reserved page (linked for more RAM than
     `--mem-size` grants) with a clear "raise --mem-size" message, instead of

- Note (2026-06-12 retitle): 128 MB is only the DEFAULT, not the limit.
  `--mem-size` sets the program RAM up to 2 GiB - 4 KiB; the driver maps that
  PLUS one 4 KiB V-transport scratch page on top (L26), so mmap = QEMU memory
  backend = vsim RAM window. The old title "must fit in the 128 MB shared
  mmap" was misleading. The real limitation is now the RUNTIME-growth fit
  check plus the 2 GiB ceiling.
- When it bites: heap, stack, or static data extends past the size in
  effect (default 128 MB), or the workload needs more than 2 GiB at all.
- What happens: the STATIC image is now checked -- a load-time guard
  (`elf_load_top` + `cmd_run.cpp`, L26/F3) rejects an ELF whose PT_LOAD
  segments reach past `--mem-size` (into the reserved scratch page) with a
  clear "raise --mem-size" message. But RUNTIME growth (heap or stack past
  the ceiling) still has no startup check: vsim's memory rejects or truncates
  the access, QEMU may see it as MMIO, and nothing names `--mem-size` as the
  cause. Separately, 2 GiB is a hard wall: the AE350 DRAM window is
  `0x00000000..0x80000000`, QEMU rejects a larger `ram_size`, and the driver
  pre-caps `--mem-size` at 2 GiB - 4 KiB (the window minus the scratch page)
  -- no setting runs a > 2 GiB workload.
- Where: `driver/cmd_run.cpp:353` (128 MB default), `:363` (2 GiB - 4 KiB
  pre-cap), `:369` (the L26/F3 static-image guard, via `driver/elf_syms.hpp`
  `elf_load_top`); `QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c` (DRAM window + ram_size
  check); `verilator/src/main.cpp` (vsim RAM window sized from
  `--shared-mem-size`).
- Status: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED. The static PT_LOAD fit check landed (L26/F3)
  and the V scratch can no longer be clobbered (it moved above program RAM,
  L26); runtime heap/stack overflow past the ceiling still corrupts silently.

# HARD GATE - read before any edit
Before calling Edit, Write, or NotebookEdit on a non-test file, you MUST:
1. Identify the smallest behavior the change adds or fixes.
2. Have an existing failing test for that behavior visible in this session,
   either by writing one in this turn OR by running the suite and showing
   its failing output. The test must reference the behavior, not just compile.
3. State which TDD phase the next edit belongs to: RED (writing the test),
   GREEN (smallest code to pass), or REFACTOR (tests already green).

If steps 1-2 are not satisfied, STOP. Do not edit the non-test file.
Instead, write the failing test first: pick the test file, draft the
smallest test that captures the behavior, run it, and confirm it fails
for the right reason. Only then proceed to the implementation edit.


This gate applies even when the user asks to "just implement X". The
correct response is to write the test first, then implement - not to
skip the test because the user did not mention it.

# ROLE AND EXPERTISE

You are a senior software engineer who follows Test-Driven Development (TDD) and Tidy First principles. Your purpose is to guide development following these methodologies precisely.

# CORE DEVELOPMENT PRINCIPLES

- Always follow the TDD cycle: Red → Green → Refactor Refactor Refacot
- Write the simplest failing test first
- Implement the minimum code needed to make tests pass
- Refactor only after tests are passing
- Maintain high code quality throughout development, always apply the modern design patterns.
* Never workaround issues! find the real root causes and apply the proper solution. No quick fix. The slowest but proper solution is the fastest solution. is the fastest solution.
* If the code snippet needs to be changed, prefer removing all of them and rewrite completely. Don't patch the legacy code. Remove them and rewrite . Don't patch the legacy code. Remove them and rewrite. 

# TDD METHODOLOGY GUIDANCE

- Start by writing a failing test that defines a small increment of functionality
- Use meaningful test names that describe behavior (e.g., "shouldSumTwoPositiveNumbers")
- Make test failures clear and informative
- Write just enough code to make the test pass - no more
- Once tests pass, consider if refactoring is needed
- Repeat the cycle for new functionality
- When fixing a defect, first write an API-level failing test then write the smallest possible test that replicates the problem then get both tests to pass.

# When refactoring the code base: TIDY FIRST APPROACH

- Separate all changes into two distinct types:
  1. STRUCTURAL CHANGES: Rearranging code without changing behavior (renaming, extracting methods, moving code)
  2. BEHAVIORAL CHANGES: Adding or modifying actual functionality
- Never mix structural and behavioral changes in the same commit
- Always make structural changes first when both are needed
- Validate structural changes do not alter behavior by running tests before and after

# COMMIT DISCIPLINE

- Only commit when:
  1. ALL tests are passing
  2. ALL compiler/linter warnings have been resolved
  3. The change represents a single logical unit of work
  4. Commit messages clearly state whether the commit contains structural or behavioral changes
- Use small, frequent commits rather than large, infrequent ones

# CODE QUALITY STANDARDS

- Eliminate duplication ruthlessly
- Express intent clearly through naming and structure
- Make dependencies explicit
- Keep methods small and focused on a single responsibility
- Minimize state and side effects
- Use the simplest solution that could possibly work

# REFACTORING GUIDELINES

- Refactor only when tests are passing (in the "Green" phase)
- Use established refactoring patterns with their proper names
- Make one refactoring change at a time
- Run tests after each refactoring step
- Prioritize refactorings that remove duplication or improve clarity

# EXAMPLE WORKFLOW

When approaching a new feature:

1. Write a simple failing test for a small part of the feature
2. Implement the bare minimum to make it pass
3. Run tests to confirm they pass (Green)
4. Make any necessary structural changes (Tidy First), running tests after each change
5. Commit structural changes separately
6. Add another test for the next small increment of functionality
7. Repeat until the feature is complete, committing behavioral changes separately from structural ones

Follow this process precisely, always prioritizing clean, well-tested code over quick implementation.

# V-scratch reservation: move the transport page out of the program's RAM

## Problem (L26)

The V-register transport stages 32 vector registers through a 4 KB guest-RAM
window at the **compile-time constant** `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` (15 MB).
That address sits *inside* the program's usable RAM, so a program that places
data there (large heap, custom linker script, direct addressing) is silently
corrupted on every resume -- even if it never uses V. Demonstrated by
`tests/fixtures/break_vscratch.S`.

## Core architecture (the fix: scheme D)

Put the scratch page **just above the program's declared RAM**, by making the
physical mmap one page larger than `--mem-size`. The program is told it has
`mem_size`; the simulator quietly maps `mem_size + 4 KB` and parks the scratch
in the extra page. No program layout can reach a page above its own ceiling
without a bug, so the collision class is removed at the root rather than
detected after the fact.

```
            +----------------+ ram_base + mmap_size            (physical top)
V scratch ->|  V scratch 4KB |   mmap_size = mem_size + 4 KB
            +----------------+ ram_base + mem_size             (program ceiling)
            |  program RAM   |   text / data / heap / stack -- all strictly below
            +----------------+ ram_base
```

Scratch GPA = `ram_base + mmap_size - kVScratchBytes` = the **top page of the
mmap**. Both legs already receive `mmap_size`, so the address stays a derived
value with **no new field to keep in sync** -- the only change vs the naive
"top of RAM" is that the mmap is one page bigger than the program's RAM, which
lifts the scratch above everything the program can legally address.

Invariant that must hold at every step: **the host stager and the vsim
Program-Buffer sweep must use the SAME scratch address.** That is why the
"runtime GPA" work (F1) lands as one atomic unit across all three users.

## Features

### F1. Runtime scratch GPA = top page of the mmap span  [state: DONE]
- Verified 2026-06-15: host unit suites green -- v_regfile_xfer 3/3,
  resume_driver 33/33, state_drain 32/32 (incl. new unset-guard tests), +18
  other hybrid suites. vsim builds all 5 CPUs. Full marker e2e 22/22 (incl. V
  fixtures + S/U ax66). `break_vscratch.elf` (the L26 repro) now PASSES under
  `--model hybrid --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium` (was a hang) -- the 0x00FF0000
  sentinel survives because the V transport relocated to the mmap top page.
- Design note: `scratch_gpa` is a required-when-V ctor arg on ResumeDriver /
  StateDrain, defaulting to a `kVScratchGpaUnset` sentinel; a V handoff that
  reaches the sweep unset throws (no silent transport via a bogus address).
  The 60+ non-V unit-test ctor sites pass a stand-in (kScratch); the real glue
  (simulator.hpp `v_scratch_gpa()`) threads the live value through the two
  controllers.
- NOT yet run as e2e: cosim / lockstep V paths (their drain_full /
  drain_checkpoint scratch logic is covered at unit level; same threading).
- Replace the fixed `kVScratchGpa` constant with `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base,
  ram_size) = ram_base + ram_size - kVScratchBytes`. The scratch is the top
  `kVScratchBytes` of whatever RAM span is mapped.
- Host stager (`stage_v_to_scratch` / `read_v_from_scratch`) computes the
  offset as `ram_size - kVScratchBytes` (it already receives the span + base).
- `ResumeDriver` / `StateDrain` take the scratch GPA as a required ctor arg
  (no silent default) and pass it to `pb_v_data_sweep`.
- `simulator.hpp` construction sites compute the GPA from
  `platform.main_memory` and pass it down.
- After F1 alone the scratch is the top page of `mem_size` (scheme A: inside
  program RAM, but far above this runtime's 7 MB stack -- already better than
  the mid-RAM 15 MB constant). F2 lifts it above program RAM (scheme D).
- Key files: `verilator/src/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `resume_driver.hpp`,
  `state_drain.hpp`, `program_buffer.hpp` (caller), `simulator.hpp`,
  `resume_from_qemu.hpp`, `handoff_controller.hpp`, `lockstep_controller.hpp`;
  tests `tests/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.test.cpp`, `resume_driver.test.cpp`,
  `state_drain.test.cpp`.
- Deps: none.

### F2. Map one page above --mem-size; scratch sits above program RAM  [state: DONE]
- Verified 2026-06-16: shared ABI gained `HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`
  (= 32*HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX); v_regfile_xfer's `kVScratchBytes` references it.
  Driver helpers `physical_mmap_bytes()` / `max_program_mem_bytes()` (shm.cpp,
  unit-tested in infra-test); `run_plan.cpp` allocates + reports the physical
  size (program + page); `cmd_run.cpp` caps --mem-size at 2G - page;
  `tests/e2e.sh` mmap split into PROGRAM_SIZE + V_SCRATCH_BYTES.
- Proof: driver builds; 9 driver unit suites + plan-itest pass; V e2e 4/4 with
  the larger mmap. NEW guard `tests/fixtures/break_vscratch_top.S` writes a
  sentinel at the program's LAST page (0x07FFF000 @128M) and PASSES under
  hybrid -- the sentinel survives the V transport, proving the scratch moved to
  the ceiling (0x08000000), above program RAM. Under F1/scheme A that page WAS
  the scratch and the fixture would hang.
- Note: only the hybrid (shared-mmap) path reserves the page; `--model fast`
  (plain `-m`, no handoff, no scratch) is untouched.
- Driver: physical mmap / QEMU backend size / vsim `--shared-mem-size` =
  `mem_size + kVScratchBytes`; the program's RAM ceiling stays `mem_size`.
- 2 GiB edge: `mem_size + 4 KB` would cross into MROM at 0x80000000, so cap
  usable `--mem-size` at `2G - 4 KB` (doc note; 2G was always approximate, L7).
- `tests/e2e.sh` shared-mmap setup must add the page too (it sizes its own
  mmap for the e2e path).
- Key files: `driver/cmd_run.cpp`, `driver/shm.cpp`, `driver/plan.*`,
  `driver/engine_registry.cpp`, `tests/e2e.sh`; driver unit tests.
- Deps: F1.

### F3. Load-time overlap check (loud abort)  [state: DONE]
- Verified 2026-06-16: `elf_load_top()` (elf_syms.cpp) returns the highest
  PT_LOAD `p_paddr + p_memsz`; `cmd_run.cpp` rejects a hybrid run when that
  exceeds the scratch GPA (ram_base + --mem-size). Unit: elf-syms test
  (load-top on a fixture + non-ELF err) + 9/9 driver suites. Integration:
  `--mem-size 1M` on a fixture linked at 0x100000 aborts with "ELF static image
  ends at 0x100036, overlapping the reserved V-transport scratch page at
  0x100000 ... raise --mem-size"; default 128M runs clean (no false positive).
- Scope: static image only (PT_LOAD). Runtime heap/stack growth into the
  scratch is already impossible under F2 (scratch is above the program ceiling).
- Reject any ELF segment (and ideally the initial SP) overlapping
  `[scratch_gpa, scratch_gpa + kVScratchBytes)`. With F2 this never fires for
  well-behaved programs; it converts the paranoid "program pokes past its own
  ceiling" case from silent corruption into a clear error.
- Key files: driver ELF loader / vsim `state_loader.hpp`; new unit test.
- Deps: F1, F2.

### F4. Docs  [state: DONE]
- Done 2026-06-16: `docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb` L26 -> RESOLVED (scheme D
  fix narrative) + quick-ref row; L10 updated (scratch GPA is now runtime-
  derived, no longer a porting blocker). `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` 2.5 (--mem-size is
  program RAM; driver maps +1 page for the scratch; cap 2G-page; ELF-overlap
  reject). `CLAUDE.md` V-State Transport (top-page GPA, required-when-V arg,
  +1-page mmap). `runtime/andes-sim.ld` comment (no fixed reservation).
- ABI DRY: `v_regfile_xfer.hpp` `kVScratchBytes` now references the shared
  `HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`; host units + vsim rebuilt green.
- `specs/hybrid-sim-gem5-switch-parity.md` (a draft gem5/virt-parity design
  archive that still cited a fixed `kVScratchGpa = 0x80FF0000`) was removed
  2026-06-16 at the user's request.
- Deps: F1, F2, F3.

1230	## 5. One binary on every engine (the vplat runtime)
1231	
1232	A binary linked with a semihosting libgloss (e.g. `-lgloss_vh`) can print
1233	only where a QEMU intercepts the semihosting `ebreak` triple; vsim has no
1234	semihosting, so a syscall inside the ROI traps there -- the old Phase-2
1235	"no syscalls inside the ROI" rule. The **vplat runtime** removes the
1236	per-engine build split: it is a newlib stub layer
1237	(`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`) that talks only to devices both
1238	engines model at the same addresses, so ONE ELF runs on `fast`, on `cycle`,
1239	and across a `hybrid` handoff, and a syscall inside the ROI works (it just
1240	adds its real cycles to the figure). Every in-tree C fixture links this
1241	runtime; nothing in the repo uses `-lgloss_vh` anymore.
1242	
1243	| Channel | Device | QEMU andes_ae350 | vsim |
1244	|---------|--------|------------------|------|
1245	| stdio (fd 0-2)   | UART2 16550, `THR` @ `0xf0300020`, `LSR` @ `0xf0300034` | `serial_mm_init` (serial0) | `src/platform/uart.hpp` |
1246	| exit code        | SimControl @ `0xe0080000` (u32 < 256 = exit code)       | `hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c` | `src/platform/sim_control.hpp` |
1247	| file io (fd > 2) | HTIF magicmem command @ `0xe0080010`                    | same device | same model |
1248	
1249	The runtime ships prebuilt as `libandes_sim_runtime.a`. Build it once
1250	(`./andes-sim build --what runtime`, or any fixture build does it implicitly),
1251	then compile with two extra flags (same line for every engine; no `-mvh`,
1252	no `-lgloss_vh`):
1253	
1254	```sh
1255	"$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
1256	  -B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
1257	```
1258	
1259	`-B` points gcc at the built artifacts (use the absolute path to
1260	`<repo>/build/runtime` when compiling outside the repo);
1261	`-specs=andes-sim.specs` swaps the startfile to the runtime's `crt0.o`,
1262	adds `-T andes-sim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and rewrites the library
1263	list to `--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc --end-group`, so no
1264	libgloss or semihosting can leak into the link.
1265	
1266	Without the gcc driver (a custom build system), link the pieces directly:
1267	
1268	```sh
1269	... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T build/runtime/andes-sim.ld \
1270	  build/runtime/crt0.o your_prog.o -L build/runtime \
1271	  -Wl,--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
1272	```
1273	
1274	Sources live in `runtime/` (crt0.S boot, trap.S + handler.c trap
1275	diagnostics, vplat_syscalls.c newlib stubs). `crt0.o` is shipped next to
1276	the archive, not inside it: nothing references `_start`, so the linker
1277	would never extract it from a `.a`.
1278	
1279	Ready-made fixtures: `vplat_hello.elf` (stdio + exit), `vplat_exit41.elf`
1280	(exit-code propagation), `vplat_file.elf` (HTIF file io); they are built
1281	with exactly the two-flag command above. Per-feature smoke tests live in
1282	`tests/vplat/test_vplat_f1..f9.sh`.
1283	
1284	Notes:
1285	
1286	- **Exit codes** stay below 256; the write to `0xe0080000` terminates the
1287	  simulation and becomes the simulator process exit code on both engines
1288	  (magic commands `0x01234567/68/71` map to 0, `0x01234569/70` to 1).
1289	- **File io** is host-passthrough: paths resolve relative to the engine
1290	  process cwd; the QEMU device mirrors vsim's `sys_call.hpp` table
1291	  byte-for-byte (newlib->Linux `O_*` translation, `st_mode`/`st_size`-only
1292	  stat writeback).
1293	- **ROI markers are safe in vplat binaries.** The markers are RISC-V HINTs
1294	  (`slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1` -- rd=x0 discards the result), so they execute
1295	  as NOPs on every engine and on silicon: one marker ELF runs standalone on
1296	  fast/cycle AND drives `--trigger marker` on hybrid. Get them from
1297	  `#include <andes_sim/ROI.h>` (`andes_sim_ROI_begin()/end()`; the header
1298	  rides the same `-B build/runtime` flag). For binaries you cannot edit,

## 5. One binary on every engine (the vplat runtime)

A binary linked with a semihosting libgloss (e.g. `-lgloss_vh`) can print
only where a QEMU intercepts the semihosting `ebreak` triple; vsim has no
semihosting, so a syscall inside the ROI traps there -- the old Phase-2
"no syscalls inside the ROI" rule. The **vplat runtime** removes the
per-engine build split: it is a newlib stub layer
(`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`) that talks only to devices both
engines model at the same addresses, so ONE ELF runs on `fast`, on `cycle`,
and across a `hybrid` handoff, and a syscall inside the ROI works (it just
adds its real cycles to the figure). Every in-tree C fixture links this
runtime; nothing in the repo uses `-lgloss_vh` anymore.

| Channel | Device | QEMU andes_ae350 | vsim |
|---------|--------|------------------|------|
| stdio (fd 0-2)   | UART2 16550, `THR` @ `0xf0300020`, `LSR` @ `0xf0300034` | `serial_mm_init` (serial0) | `src/platform/uart.hpp` |
| exit code        | SimControl @ `0xe0080000` (u32 < 256 = exit code)       | `hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c` | `src/platform/sim_control.hpp` |
| file io (fd > 2) | HTIF magicmem command @ `0xe0080010`                    | same device | same model |

The runtime ships prebuilt as `libandes_sim_runtime.a`. Build it once
(`./andes-sim build --what runtime`, or any fixture build does it implicitly),
then compile with two extra flags (same line for every engine; no `-mvh`,
no `-lgloss_vh`):

```sh
"$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
  -B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
```

`-B` points gcc at the built artifacts (use the absolute path to
`<repo>/build/runtime` when compiling outside the repo);
`-specs=andes-sim.specs` swaps the startfile to the runtime's `crt0.o`,
adds `-T andes-sim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and rewrites the library
list to `--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc --end-group`, so no
libgloss or semihosting can leak into the link.

Without the gcc driver (a custom build system), link the pieces directly:

```sh
... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T build/runtime/andes-sim.ld \
  build/runtime/crt0.o your_prog.o -L build/runtime \
  -Wl,--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
```

Sources live in `runtime/` (crt0.S boot, trap.S + handler.c trap
diagnostics, vplat_syscalls.c newlib stubs). `crt0.o` is shipped next to
the archive, not inside it: nothing references `_start`, so the linker
would never extract it from a `.a`.

Ready-made fixtures: `vplat_hello.elf` (stdio + exit), `vplat_exit41.elf`
(exit-code propagation), `vplat_file.elf` (HTIF file io); they are built
with exactly the two-flag command above. Per-feature smoke tests live in
`tests/vplat/test_vplat_f1..f9.sh`.

Notes:

- **Exit codes** stay below 256; the write to `0xe0080000` terminates the
  simulation and becomes the simulator process exit code on both engines
  (magic commands `0x01234567/68/71` map to 0, `0x01234569/70` to 1).
- **File io** is host-passthrough: paths resolve relative to the engine
  process cwd; the QEMU device mirrors vsim's `sys_call.hpp` table
  byte-for-byte (newlib->Linux `O_*` translation, `st_mode`/`st_size`-only
  stat writeback).
- **ROI markers are safe in vplat binaries.** The markers are RISC-V HINTs
  (`slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1` -- rd=x0 discards the result), so they execute
  as NOPs on every engine and on silicon: one marker ELF runs standalone on
  fast/cycle AND drives `--trigger marker` on hybrid. Get them from
  `#include <andes_sim/ROI.h>` (`andes_sim_ROI_begin()/end()`; the header
  rides the same `-B build/runtime` flag). For binaries you cannot edit,
  delimit the ROI with PC symbols and `--trigger pc` instead (see
  `tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.c`: `say_hello` / `vplat_roi_end`).
- A `printf` inside the measured window now works (the UART is modeled and
  its MMIO cost is real), but it still adds those UART cycles to the figure -
  keep measured kernels I/O-free when you care about clean numbers.
- `docs/andes_sim_tutorial.ipynb` sections 2, 3 and 4d run the same
  `hello.elf` through all three models.

---

content.text:
The trick: link against the **vplat runtime** instead of semihosting. One ELF then runs on `fast`, `cycle`, and `hybrid` because the runtime only talks to MMIO devices that all three engines model at the same addresses. No `-mvh`, no `-lgloss_vh`.

## Compile once

```sh
"$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
  -B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
```

Two flags do everything:
- `-B build/runtime` - tells gcc where the runtime artifacts are (use the absolute path if you compile outside the repo).
- `-specs=andes-sim.specs` - swaps in the runtime's `crt0.o`, the linker script `andes-sim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and rewrites the lib list so no semihosting can leak in.

Then run the same file three ways:
```sh
./andes-sim run --model fast   your_prog.elf
./andes-sim run --model cycle  your_prog.elf
./andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger marker your_prog.elf
```

## How the three I/O channels work

Each C library call bottoms out in a device both engines have at one fixed address (`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`):

| What you call | Where it goes | Address |
|---|---|---|
| `printf` / stdout / stderr (fd 0-2) | UART2 16550, byte at a time | THR `0xf0300020`, LSR `0xf0300034` |
| `exit(code)` | SimControl, write a u32 < 256 | `0xe0080000` |
| `fopen`/`read`/`write` to a real file (fd > 2) | HTIF magic-mem, served by the host | `0xe0080010` |

**Printf** - `_write` for fd 0-2 just pushes each character to the UART (`uart_putc`). stdout and stderr use the same UART, so error messages print the same way as normal output. Works on every engine; inside a measured ROI it still works but adds real UART cycles to the count, so keep hot kernels I/O-free.

**Error / crash** - if the program traps (bad load, illegal insn), `trap.S` + `handler.c` catch it and print a register/cause diagnostic over the same UART, then exit. So a crash is visible, not silent, on all three engines.

**File IO** - for fd > 2, `_open`/`_read`/`_write`/`_close`/`_fstat` send an HTIF command to `0xe0080010`; the engine serves it host-side (paths are relative to the engine process cwd). QEMU's device mirrors vsim's `sys_call.hpp` table byte-for-byte, so the same file behavior holds across the handoff.

Ready-made examples: `vplat_hello.elf` (stdio+exit), `vplat_exit41.elf` (exit code), `vplat_file.elf` (file io). Full reference: `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` section 5.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F6 contract: `scripts/run_e2e.sh` works out of the box -- its default
# VSIM_BIN must be the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine
# (sim_ax45mpv_premium, the same default ./andes-sim pins), NOT the
# alphabetically-first verilator/build/sim_* (sim_ax45mpv_mp2, a 2-core
# config where crt0's secondary-hart SKIPPED write stops the sim before
# hart 0 drains and every C fixture fails).
#
# The probe: one marker e2e fixture with NO VSIM_BIN in the environment.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

[ -x "$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium" ] || fail "premium engine not built"
[ -x "$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_mp2" ] \
  || echo "[note] mp2 engine absent; default-pick ambiguity not present on this host"

  >/tmp/vplat_f6_run.log 2>&1 \
  || fail "default-engine e2e rt_c_hello[marker] failed (picked a multi-hart engine?): $(tail -4 /tmp/vplat_f6_run.log)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runtime-lib F2 contract: `make -C runtime` produces a linkable library
# under build/runtime/ so users stop listing the 4 runtime sources:
#
#   build/runtime/libandes_sim_runtime.a   (trap.o handler.o vplat_syscalls.o)
#   build/runtime/crt0.o                   (startfile; OUTSIDE the archive)
#   build/runtime/andes-sim.ld             (linker script)
#
# Probe: link vplat_hello.c with the raw library line (no specs file yet)
# and run it on the cycle engine -- prints via UART, exits 0 via SimControl.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"
NM="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm"

SIM="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not built: $SIM"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime" || fail "runtime lib build failed"

RT="$ROOT/build/runtime"
[ -f "$RT/libandes_sim_runtime.a" ] || fail "missing $RT/libandes_sim_runtime.a"
[ -f "$RT/crt0.o" ] || fail "missing $RT/crt0.o"
[ -f "$RT/andes-sim.ld" ] || fail "missing $RT/andes-sim.ld"

# crt0 must be a standalone startfile: the archive never gets _start pulled.
# (grep without -q: early-exit + pipefail turns a MATCH into SIGPIPE failure)
"$NM" "$RT/crt0.o" | grep ' T _start' >/dev/null \
  || fail "crt0.o does not define _start"
"$NM" "$RT/libandes_sim_runtime.a" | grep ' T _write' >/dev/null \
  || fail "archive does not define _write"
"$NM" "$RT/libandes_sim_runtime.a" | grep ' T m_trap_entry' >/dev/null \
  || fail "archive does not define m_trap_entry"

# Raw (non-specs) link: what a non-gcc-driver build system would write.
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs \
  -T "$RT/andes-sim.ld" "$RT/crt0.o" "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.c" \
  -L "$RT" -Wl,--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group \
  -o "$TMP/hello.elf" || fail "raw -landes_sim_runtime link failed"

OUT=$(timeout 120 "$SIM" "$TMP/hello.elf" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from vplat' \
  || fail "cycle: missing 'hello from vplat' in: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "cycle: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

# and run it on the cycle engine -- prints via UART, exits 0 via SimControl.

ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

[ -f "$RT/libandes_sim_runtime.a" ] || fail "missing $RT/libandes_sim_runtime.a"

[ -f "$RT/andes-sim.ld" ] || fail "missing $RT/andes-sim.ld"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Author docs/andes_sim_runtime_tutorial.ipynb (empty outputs).

Cells are clean source strings here; nbconvert fills outputs next,
then canon_nb.py canonicalizes to the repo's notebook convention.
"""
import json

def md(text):
    return {"cell_type": "markdown", "metadata": {},
            "source": text.splitlines(keepends=True)}

def code(text):
    return {"cell_type": "code", "execution_count": None, "metadata": {},
            "outputs": [], "source": text.splitlines(keepends=True)}

cells = []

cells.append(md(
"""# andes-sim tutorial: one binary, every engine (the vplat runtime)

A binary linked against a semihosting libgloss (`-lgloss_vh`) can only
do I/O where QEMU intercepts the semihosting trap. vsim has no
semihosting, so that same binary stalls the moment it calls `printf` on
the cycle engine - the old "no syscalls inside the measured region"
rule.

The **vplat runtime** removes that split. It is a small newlib stub
layer (`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`) that talks only to MMIO devices
**both** engines model at the **same** addresses, so ONE ELF runs
unchanged on `fast`, on `cycle`, and across a `hybrid` handoff.

| Channel | Device | Address |
|---------|--------|---------|
| stdout / stderr (fd 0-2) | UART2 16550 | THR `0xf0300020`, LSR `0xf0300034` |
| exit code | SimControl | `0xe0080000` (write a u32 < 256) |
| file io (fd > 2) | HTIF magic-mem | `0xe0080010`, served host-side |

This tutorial builds ONE binary and shows the things you need from a
C program working the same on every engine:

1. compile once, run on `fast` / `cycle` / `hybrid` (stdout, stderr, exit code),
2. an error / trap -> the runtime's trap handler,
3. file io -> the host filesystem via HTIF.
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""import os
from pathlib import Path
root = next(str(d) for d in (Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents)
            if (d / "build" / "andes-sim").exists())
os.chdir(root)
os.environ["PATH"] = f"{root}/build:" + os.environ["PATH"]
print("working dir:", root)
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""## 1. The two flags

The runtime ships prebuilt as `build/runtime/libandes_sim_runtime.a`
(any fixture build makes it, or `./andes-sim build --what runtime`). You
compile with two extra flags - the SAME line for every engine, no
`-mvh`, no `-lgloss_vh`:

    -B build/runtime         # find crt0.o, the linker script, the archive
    -specs=andes-sim.specs   # swap in that startfile + rewrite the lib list

`-specs` swaps the startfile to the runtime's `crt0.o`, adds
`-T andes-sim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and rewrites the library
list to `--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc --end-group`, so no
semihosting can leak into the link. Compiling outside the repo, use the
absolute path to `<repo>/build/runtime` for `-B`.
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""## 2. Compile once, run on three engines

One program, one compile command. It prints to **stdout** and to
**stderr**, runs a trivial loop wrapped in the ROI markers (free HINT
NOPs from `<andes_sim/ROI.h>`, so the binary still runs everywhere), and
returns an exit code.
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
. ./config.env 2>/dev/null      # sets HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"

cat > io_demo.c <<'EOF'
/* One binary for every engine: stdout, stderr, an ROI, an exit code.
 * No semihosting - the two link flags route I/O to MMIO devices both
 * the QEMU (fast) and vsim (cycle) engines model. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <andes_sim/ROI.h>

int main(void)
{
  printf("hello on stdout\\n");            /* fd 1 -> UART */
  fprintf(stderr, "status on stderr\\n");  /* fd 2 -> UART */

  andes_sim_ROI_begin();                  /* free HINT NOPs */
  long sum = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < 1000; i++) sum += i;
  andes_sim_ROI_end();

  printf("sum = %ld\\n", sum);
  return 0;                               /* -> SimControl: process exit 0 */
}
EOF

"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \\
  -B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs io_demo.c -o io_demo.elf

echo "built:"; file io_demo.elf
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""**fast** (QEMU, functional) runs it in well under a second. `andes-sim`
forwards the program's exit code as its own process exit code, so a shell
can branch on it:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
andes-sim run --model fast io_demo.elf
echo "process exit: $?"
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""**cycle** runs the WHOLE program on the RTL engine. Same source, same
ELF - only `--model` changed. The stdout/stderr text is byte-identical;
the engine adds its own `[info]` lines and a final cycle total.
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""!andes-sim run --model cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium io_demo.elf
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""**hybrid** fast-forwards on QEMU, then measures the ROI on the RTL. The
markers compiled into the binary above drive `--trigger marker`. stdout
and stderr still print (they run before the window); the final `sum =`
line belongs to the fast leg, so in hybrid the run stops at the exit
marker before printing it.
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""!andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium io_demo.elf
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""## 3. Errors: the trap handler

The runtime installs a machine-mode trap handler (`runtime/trap.S` +
`handler.c`). Any unexpected trap - illegal instruction, bad access -
prints a red `[ERROR]` diagnostic (mcause / mepc / mtval) to stderr and
calls `_exit(mcause)`, which SimControl turns into the process exit
code. This program runs one illegal instruction on purpose:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
. ./config.env 2>/dev/null
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"

cat > trap_demo.c <<'EOF'
#include <stdio.h>
int main(void)
{
  printf("about to run an illegal instruction\\n");
  __asm__ __volatile__(".word 0x00000000");  /* illegal -> trap */
  printf("this line never runs\\n");
  return 0;
}
EOF

"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \\
  -B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs trap_demo.c -o trap_demo.elf
echo "built trap_demo.elf"
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""On **fast**, the handler catches it: `mcause: 0x2` is "illegal
instruction", and the process exits with that code (2), not 0:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
andes-sim run --model fast trap_demo.elf
echo "process exit: $?"
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""The **cycle** engine has the same handler and produces the same
diagnostic and the same exit code - the trap path is part of the
portable runtime, not the simulator:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
andes-sim run --model cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium trap_demo.elf
echo "process exit: $?"
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""## 4. File io: the host filesystem

For fd > 2 the stubs forward `open`/`read`/`write`/`close`/`fstat` to
the HTIF magic-mem device, which the engine serves on the host. Paths
resolve relative to the **engine process's working directory** (here,
the repo root). This program writes a file and reads it back:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
. ./config.env 2>/dev/null
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"

cat > fileio_demo.c <<'EOF'
#include <stdio.h>
int main(void)
{
  const char *path = "io_demo_file.txt";

  FILE *f = fopen(path, "w");
  if (!f) { printf("fopen(w) failed\\n"); return 1; }
  fprintf(f, "written by the guest, read back by the guest\\n");
  fclose(f);

  char line[80] = {0};
  f = fopen(path, "r");
  if (!f) { printf("fopen(r) failed\\n"); return 1; }
  fgets(line, sizeof line, f);
  fclose(f);

  printf("read back: %s", line);
  return 0;
}
EOF

"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \\
  -B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs fileio_demo.c -o fileio_demo.elf
echo "built fileio_demo.elf"
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""Run on **fast**, then look at the host directory - the guest's file is
really there:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
andes-sim run --model fast fileio_demo.elf
echo "--- the host now has the file (engine cwd = $(pwd)) ---"
cat io_demo_file.txt
rm -f io_demo_file.txt
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""The same ELF on **cycle** produces the same file - the QEMU device and
the vsim model serve the HTIF syscall table byte-for-byte:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
andes-sim run --model cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium fileio_demo.elf
echo "--- host file after the cycle run ---"
cat io_demo_file.txt
rm -f io_demo_file.txt
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""## Recap

| You want | How |
|----------|-----|
| One portable ELF | compile with `-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs` (no `-lgloss_vh`) |
| Run it three ways | `andes-sim run --model fast\\|cycle\\|hybrid ... your.elf` |
| `printf` / stderr | write to fd 0-2; the runtime drives the UART |
| Exit code | `return n;` (n < 256) -> SimControl -> process exit code |
| Catch a crash | the runtime's trap handler prints `[ERROR]` + exits `mcause` |
| Read/write a file | normal stdio on fd > 2 -> HTIF, served in the engine's cwd |

The ROI markers are free HINT NOPs, so a binary built this way runs
standalone on silicon AND drives `--trigger marker` on hybrid. For a
binary you cannot edit, delimit the region with PC symbols and
`--trigger pc` instead.

More: `docs/andes_sim_demo.ipynb` (model tour),
`docs/andes_sim_gemm_tutorial.ipynb` (cycle measurement),
`docs/USER_GUIDE.md` section 5 (full runtime reference).
"""))

nb = {"cells": cells,
      "metadata": {"kernelspec": {"display_name": "Python 3 (ipykernel)",
                                  "language": "python", "name": "python3"},
                   "language_info": {"name": "python"}},
      "nbformat": 4, "nbformat_minor": 4}

with open("docs/andes_sim_runtime_tutorial.ipynb", "w") as fh:
    json.dump(nb, fh, indent=1)
    fh.write("\n")
print("wrote docs/andes_sim_runtime_tutorial.ipynb with", len(cells), "cells")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Author docs/andes_sim_runtime_tutorial.ipynb (empty outputs).

Cells are clean source strings here; nbconvert fills outputs next,
then canon_nb.py canonicalizes to the repo's notebook convention.
"""
import json

def md(text):
    return {"cell_type": "markdown", "metadata": {},
            "source": text.splitlines(keepends=True)}

def code(text):
    return {"cell_type": "code", "execution_count": None, "metadata": {},
            "outputs": [], "source": text.splitlines(keepends=True)}

cells = []

cells.append(md(
"""# andes-sim tutorial: one binary, every engine (the vplat runtime)

A binary linked against a semihosting libgloss (`-lgloss_vh`) can only
do I/O where QEMU intercepts the semihosting trap. vsim has no
semihosting, so that same binary stalls the moment it calls `printf` on
the cycle engine - the old "no syscalls inside the measured region"
rule.

The **vplat runtime** removes that split. It is a small newlib stub
layer (`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`) that talks only to MMIO devices
**both** engines model at the **same** addresses, so ONE ELF runs
unchanged on `fast`, on `cycle`, and across a `hybrid` handoff.

| Channel | Device | Address |
|---------|--------|---------|
| stdout / stderr (fd 0-2) | UART2 16550 | THR `0xf0300020`, LSR `0xf0300034` |
| exit code | SimControl | `0xe0080000` (write a u32 < 256) |
| file io (fd > 2) | HTIF magic-mem | `0xe0080010`, served host-side |

This tutorial builds ONE binary and shows the things you need from a
C program working the same on every engine:

1. compile once, run on `fast` / `cycle` / `hybrid` (stdout, stderr, exit code),
2. an error / trap -> the runtime's trap handler,
3. file io -> the host filesystem via HTIF.
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""import os
from pathlib import Path
root = next(str(d) for d in (Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents)
            if (d / "build" / "andes-sim").exists())
os.chdir(root)
os.environ["PATH"] = f"{root}/build:" + os.environ["PATH"]
print("working dir:", root)
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""## 1. The two flags

The runtime ships prebuilt as `build/runtime/libandes_sim_runtime.a`
(any fixture build makes it, or `./andes-sim build --what runtime`). You
compile with two extra flags - the SAME line for every engine, no
`-mvh`, no `-lgloss_vh`:

    -B build/runtime         # find crt0.o, the linker script, the archive
    -specs=andes-sim.specs   # swap in that startfile + rewrite the lib list

`-specs` swaps the startfile to the runtime's `crt0.o`, adds
`-T andes-sim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and rewrites the library
list to `--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc --end-group`, so no
semihosting can leak into the link. Compiling outside the repo, use the
absolute path to `<repo>/build/runtime` for `-B`.
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""## 2. Compile once, run on three engines

One program, one compile command. It prints to **stdout** and to
**stderr**, runs a trivial loop wrapped in the ROI markers (free HINT
NOPs from `<andes_sim/ROI.h>`, so the binary still runs everywhere), and
returns an exit code.
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
. ./config.env 2>/dev/null      # sets HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"

cat > io_demo.c <<'EOF'
/* One binary for every engine: stdout, stderr, an ROI, an exit code.
 * No semihosting - the two link flags route I/O to MMIO devices both
 * the QEMU (fast) and vsim (cycle) engines model. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <andes_sim/ROI.h>

int main(void)
{
  printf("hello on stdout\\n");            /* fd 1 -> UART */
  fprintf(stderr, "status on stderr\\n");  /* fd 2 -> UART */

  andes_sim_ROI_begin();                  /* free HINT NOPs */
  long sum = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < 1000; i++) sum += i;
  andes_sim_ROI_end();

  printf("sum = %ld\\n", sum);
  return 0;                               /* -> SimControl: process exit 0 */
}
EOF

"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \\
  -B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs io_demo.c -o io_demo.elf

echo "built:"; file io_demo.elf
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""**fast** (QEMU, functional) runs it in well under a second. `andes-sim`
forwards the program's exit code as its own process exit code, so a shell
can branch on it:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
andes-sim run --model fast io_demo.elf
echo "process exit: $?"
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""**cycle** runs the WHOLE program on the RTL engine. Same source, same
ELF - only `--model` changed. The stdout/stderr text is byte-identical;
the engine adds its own `[info]` lines and a final cycle total.
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""!andes-sim run --model cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium io_demo.elf
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""**hybrid** fast-forwards on QEMU, then measures the ROI on the RTL. The
markers compiled into the binary above drive `--trigger marker`. stdout
and stderr still print (they run before the window); the final `sum =`
line belongs to the fast leg, so in hybrid the run stops at the exit
marker before printing it.
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""!andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium io_demo.elf
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""## 3. Errors: the trap handler

The runtime installs a machine-mode trap handler (`runtime/trap.S` +
`handler.c`). Any unexpected trap - illegal instruction, bad access -
prints a red `[ERROR]` diagnostic (mcause / mepc / mtval) to stderr and
calls `_exit(mcause)`, which SimControl turns into the process exit
code. This program runs one illegal instruction on purpose:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
. ./config.env 2>/dev/null
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"

cat > trap_demo.c <<'EOF'
#include <stdio.h>
int main(void)
{
  printf("about to run an illegal instruction\\n");
  __asm__ __volatile__(".word 0x00000000");  /* illegal -> trap */
  printf("this line never runs\\n");
  return 0;
}
EOF

"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \\
  -B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs trap_demo.c -o trap_demo.elf
echo "built trap_demo.elf"
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""On **fast**, the handler catches it: `mcause: 0x2` is "illegal
instruction", and the process exits with that code (2), not 0:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
andes-sim run --model fast trap_demo.elf
echo "process exit: $?"
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""The **cycle** engine has the same handler and produces the same
diagnostic and the same exit code - the trap path is part of the
portable runtime, not the simulator:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
andes-sim run --model cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium trap_demo.elf
echo "process exit: $?"
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""## 4. File io: the host filesystem

For fd > 2 the stubs forward `open`/`read`/`write`/`close`/`fstat` to
the HTIF magic-mem device, which the engine serves on the host. Paths
resolve relative to the **engine process's working directory** (here,
the repo root). This program writes a file and reads it back:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
. ./config.env 2>/dev/null
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"

cat > fileio_demo.c <<'EOF'
#include <stdio.h>
int main(void)
{
  const char *path = "io_demo_file.txt";

  FILE *f = fopen(path, "w");
  if (!f) { printf("fopen(w) failed\\n"); return 1; }
  fprintf(f, "written by the guest, read back by the guest\\n");
  fclose(f);

  char line[80] = {0};
  f = fopen(path, "r");
  if (!f) { printf("fopen(r) failed\\n"); return 1; }
  fgets(line, sizeof line, f);
  fclose(f);

  printf("read back: %s", line);
  return 0;
}
EOF

"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \\
  -B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs fileio_demo.c -o fileio_demo.elf
echo "built fileio_demo.elf"
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""Run on **fast**, then look at the host directory - the guest's file is
really there:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
andes-sim run --model fast fileio_demo.elf
echo "--- the host now has the file (engine cwd = $(pwd)) ---"
cat io_demo_file.txt
rm -f io_demo_file.txt
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""The same ELF on **cycle** produces the same file - the QEMU device and
the vsim model serve the HTIF syscall table byte-for-byte:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
andes-sim run --model cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium fileio_demo.elf
echo "--- host file after the cycle run ---"
cat io_demo_file.txt
rm -f io_demo_file.txt
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""## Recap

| You want | How |
|----------|-----|
| One portable ELF | compile with `-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs` (no `-lgloss_vh`) |
| Run it three ways | `andes-sim run --model fast\\|cycle\\|hybrid ... your.elf` |
| `printf` / stderr | write to fd 0-2; the runtime drives the UART |
| Exit code | `return n;` (n < 256) -> SimControl -> process exit code |
| Catch a crash | the runtime's trap handler prints `[ERROR]` + exits `mcause` |
| Read/write a file | normal stdio on fd > 2 -> HTIF, served in the engine's cwd |

The ROI markers are free HINT NOPs, so a binary built this way runs
standalone on silicon AND drives `--trigger marker` on hybrid. For a
binary you cannot edit, delimit the region with PC symbols and
`--trigger pc` instead.

More: `docs/andes_sim_demo.ipynb` (model tour),
`docs/andes_sim_gemm_tutorial.ipynb` (cycle measurement),
`docs/USER_GUIDE.md` section 5 (full runtime reference).
"""))

nb = {"cells": cells,
      "metadata": {"kernelspec": {"display_name": "Python 3 (ipykernel)",
                                  "language": "python", "name": "python3"},
                   "language_info": {"name": "python"}},
      "nbformat": 4, "nbformat_minor": 4}

with open("docs/andes_sim_runtime_tutorial.ipynb", "w") as fh:
    json.dump(nb, fh, indent=1)
    fh.write("\n")
print("wrote docs/andes_sim_runtime_tutorial.ipynb with", len(cells), "cells")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Author docs/andes_sim_runtime_tutorial.ipynb (empty outputs).

Cells are clean source strings here; nbconvert fills outputs next,
then canon_nb.py canonicalizes to the repo's notebook convention.
"""
import json

def md(text):
    return {"cell_type": "markdown", "metadata": {},
            "source": text.splitlines(keepends=True)}

def code(text):
    return {"cell_type": "code", "execution_count": None, "metadata": {},
            "outputs": [], "source": text.splitlines(keepends=True)}

cells = []

cells.append(md(
"""# andes-sim tutorial: one binary, every engine (the vplat runtime)

A binary linked against a semihosting libgloss (`-lgloss_vh`) can only
do I/O where QEMU intercepts the semihosting trap. vsim has no
semihosting, so that same binary stalls the moment it calls `printf` on
the cycle engine - the old "no syscalls inside the measured region"
rule.

The **vplat runtime** removes that split. It is a small newlib stub
layer (`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`) that talks only to MMIO devices
**both** engines model at the **same** addresses, so ONE ELF runs
unchanged on `fast`, on `cycle`, and across a `hybrid` handoff.

| Channel | Device | Address |
|---------|--------|---------|
| stdout / stderr (fd 0-2) | UART2 16550 | THR `0xf0300020`, LSR `0xf0300034` |
| exit code | SimControl | `0xe0080000` (write a u32 < 256) |
| file io (fd > 2) | HTIF magic-mem | `0xe0080010`, served host-side |

This tutorial builds ONE binary and shows the things you need from a
C program working the same on every engine:

1. compile once, run on `fast` / `cycle` / `hybrid` (stdout, stderr, exit code),
2. an error / trap -> the runtime's trap handler,
3. file io -> the host filesystem via HTIF.
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""import os
from pathlib import Path
root = next(str(d) for d in (Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents)
            if (d / "build" / "andes-sim").exists())
os.chdir(root)
os.environ["PATH"] = f"{root}/build:" + os.environ["PATH"]
print("working dir:", root)
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""## 1. The two flags

The runtime ships prebuilt as `build/runtime/libandes_sim_runtime.a`
(any fixture build makes it, or `./andes-sim build --what runtime`). You
compile with two extra flags - the SAME line for every engine, no
`-mvh`, no `-lgloss_vh`:

    -B build/runtime         # find crt0.o, the linker script, the archive
    -specs=andes-sim.specs   # swap in that startfile + rewrite the lib list

`-specs` swaps the startfile to the runtime's `crt0.o`, adds
`-T andes-sim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and rewrites the library
list to `--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc --end-group`, so no
semihosting can leak into the link. Compiling outside the repo, use the
absolute path to `<repo>/build/runtime` for `-B`.
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""## 2. Compile once, run on three engines

One program, one compile command. It prints to **stdout** and to
**stderr**, runs a trivial loop wrapped in the ROI markers (free HINT
NOPs from `<andes_sim/ROI.h>`, so the binary still runs everywhere), and
returns an exit code.
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
. ./config.env 2>/dev/null      # sets HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"

cat > io_demo.c <<'EOF'
/* One binary for every engine: stdout, stderr, an ROI, an exit code.
 * No semihosting - the two link flags route I/O to MMIO devices both
 * the QEMU (fast) and vsim (cycle) engines model. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <andes_sim/ROI.h>

int main(void)
{
  printf("hello on stdout\\n");            /* fd 1 -> UART */
  fprintf(stderr, "status on stderr\\n");  /* fd 2 -> UART */

  andes_sim_ROI_begin();                  /* free HINT NOPs */
  long sum = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < 1000; i++) sum += i;
  andes_sim_ROI_end();

  printf("sum = %ld\\n", sum);
  return 0;                               /* -> SimControl: process exit 0 */
}
EOF

"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \\
  -B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs io_demo.c -o io_demo.elf

echo "built:"; file io_demo.elf
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""**fast** (QEMU, functional) runs it in well under a second. `andes-sim`
forwards the program's exit code as its own process exit code, so a shell
can branch on it:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
andes-sim run --model fast io_demo.elf </dev/null
echo "process exit: $?"
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""**cycle** runs the WHOLE program on the RTL engine. Same source, same
ELF - only `--model` changed. The stdout/stderr text is byte-identical;
the engine adds its own `[info]` lines and a final cycle total.
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""!andes-sim run --model cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium io_demo.elf
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""**hybrid** fast-forwards on QEMU, then measures the ROI on the RTL. The
markers compiled into the binary above drive `--trigger marker`. stdout
and stderr still print (they run before the window); the final `sum =`
line belongs to the fast leg, so in hybrid the run stops at the exit
marker before printing it.
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""!andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium io_demo.elf
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""## 3. Errors: the trap handler

The runtime installs a machine-mode trap handler (`runtime/trap.S` +
`handler.c`). Any unexpected trap - illegal instruction, bad access -
prints a red `[ERROR]` diagnostic (mcause / mepc / mtval) to stderr and
calls `_exit(mcause)`, which SimControl turns into the process exit
code. This program runs one illegal instruction on purpose:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
. ./config.env 2>/dev/null
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"

cat > trap_demo.c <<'EOF'
#include <stdio.h>
int main(void)
{
  printf("about to run an illegal instruction\\n");
  __asm__ __volatile__(".word 0x00000000");  /* illegal -> trap */
  printf("this line never runs\\n");
  return 0;
}
EOF

"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \\
  -B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs trap_demo.c -o trap_demo.elf
echo "built trap_demo.elf"
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""On **fast**, the handler catches it: `mcause: 0x2` is "illegal
instruction", and the process exits with that code (2), not 0:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
andes-sim run --model fast trap_demo.elf </dev/null
echo "process exit: $?"
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""The **cycle** engine has the same handler and produces the same
diagnostic and the same exit code - the trap path is part of the
portable runtime, not the simulator:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
andes-sim run --model cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium trap_demo.elf </dev/null
echo "process exit: $?"
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""## 4. File io: the host filesystem

For fd > 2 the stubs forward `open`/`read`/`write`/`close`/`fstat` to
the HTIF magic-mem device, which the engine serves on the host. Paths
resolve relative to the **engine process's working directory** (here,
the repo root). This program writes a file and reads it back:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
. ./config.env 2>/dev/null
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"

cat > fileio_demo.c <<'EOF'
#include <stdio.h>
int main(void)
{
  const char *path = "io_demo_file.txt";

  FILE *f = fopen(path, "w");
  if (!f) { printf("fopen(w) failed\\n"); return 1; }
  fprintf(f, "written by the guest, read back by the guest\\n");
  fclose(f);

  char line[80] = {0};
  f = fopen(path, "r");
  if (!f) { printf("fopen(r) failed\\n"); return 1; }
  fgets(line, sizeof line, f);
  fclose(f);

  printf("read back: %s", line);
  return 0;
}
EOF

"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \\
  -B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs fileio_demo.c -o fileio_demo.elf
echo "built fileio_demo.elf"
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""Run on **fast**, then look at the host directory - the guest's file is
really there:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
andes-sim run --model fast fileio_demo.elf </dev/null
echo "--- the host now has the file (engine cwd = $(pwd)) ---"
cat io_demo_file.txt
rm -f io_demo_file.txt
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""The same ELF on **cycle** produces the same file - the QEMU device and
the vsim model serve the HTIF syscall table byte-for-byte:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
andes-sim run --model cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium fileio_demo.elf </dev/null
echo "--- host file after the cycle run ---"
cat io_demo_file.txt
rm -f io_demo_file.txt
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""## Recap

| You want | How |
|----------|-----|
| One portable ELF | compile with `-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs` (no `-lgloss_vh`) |
| Run it three ways | `andes-sim run --model fast\\|cycle\\|hybrid ... your.elf` |
| `printf` / stderr | write to fd 0-2; the runtime drives the UART |
| Exit code | `return n;` (n < 256) -> SimControl -> process exit code |
| Catch a crash | the runtime's trap handler prints `[ERROR]` + exits `mcause` |
| Read/write a file | normal stdio on fd > 2 -> HTIF, served in the engine's cwd |

The ROI markers are free HINT NOPs, so a binary built this way runs
standalone on silicon AND drives `--trigger marker` on hybrid. For a
binary you cannot edit, delimit the region with PC symbols and
`--trigger pc` instead.

More: `docs/andes_sim_demo.ipynb` (model tour),
`docs/andes_sim_gemm_tutorial.ipynb` (cycle measurement),
`docs/USER_GUIDE.md` section 5 (full runtime reference).
"""))

nb = {"cells": cells,
      "metadata": {"kernelspec": {"display_name": "Python 3 (ipykernel)",
                                  "language": "python", "name": "python3"},
                   "language_info": {"name": "python"}},
      "nbformat": 4, "nbformat_minor": 4}

with open("docs/andes_sim_runtime_tutorial.ipynb", "w") as fh:
    json.dump(nb, fh, indent=1)
    fh.write("\n")
print("wrote docs/andes_sim_runtime_tutorial.ipynb with", len(cells), "cells")

# V-scratch reservation: move the transport page out of the program's RAM

## Problem (L26)

The V-register transport stages 32 vector registers through a 4 KB guest-RAM
window at the **compile-time constant** `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` (15 MB).
That address sits *inside* the program's usable RAM, so a program that places
data there (large heap, custom linker script, direct addressing) is silently
corrupted on every resume -- even if it never uses V. Demonstrated by
`tests/fixtures/break_vscratch.S`.

## Core architecture (the fix: scheme D)

Put the scratch page **just above the program's declared RAM**, by making the
physical mmap one page larger than `--mem-size`. The program is told it has
`mem_size`; the simulator quietly maps `mem_size + 4 KB` and parks the scratch
in the extra page. No program layout can reach a page above its own ceiling
without a bug, so the collision class is removed at the root rather than
detected after the fact.

```
            +----------------+ ram_base + mmap_size            (physical top)
V scratch ->|  V scratch 4KB |   mmap_size = mem_size + 4 KB
            +----------------+ ram_base + mem_size             (program ceiling)
            |  program RAM   |   text / data / heap / stack -- all strictly below
            +----------------+ ram_base
```

Scratch GPA = `ram_base + mmap_size - kVScratchBytes` = the **top page of the
mmap**. Both legs already receive `mmap_size`, so the address stays a derived
value with **no new field to keep in sync** -- the only change vs the naive
"top of RAM" is that the mmap is one page bigger than the program's RAM, which
lifts the scratch above everything the program can legally address.

Invariant that must hold at every step: **the host stager and the vsim
Program-Buffer sweep must use the SAME scratch address.** That is why the
"runtime GPA" work (F1) lands as one atomic unit across all three users.

## Features

### F1. Runtime scratch GPA = top page of the mmap span  [state: DONE]
- Verified 2026-06-15: host unit suites green -- v_regfile_xfer 3/3,
  resume_driver 33/33, state_drain 32/32 (incl. new unset-guard tests), +18
  other hybrid suites. vsim builds all 5 CPUs. Full marker e2e 22/22 (incl. V
  fixtures + S/U ax66). `break_vscratch.elf` (the L26 repro) now PASSES under
  `--model hybrid --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium` (was a hang) -- the 0x00FF0000
  sentinel survives because the V transport relocated to the mmap top page.
- Design note: `scratch_gpa` is a required-when-V ctor arg on ResumeDriver /
  StateDrain, defaulting to a `kVScratchGpaUnset` sentinel; a V handoff that
  reaches the sweep unset throws (no silent transport via a bogus address).
  The 60+ non-V unit-test ctor sites pass a stand-in (kScratch); the real glue
  (simulator.hpp `v_scratch_gpa()`) threads the live value through the two
  controllers.
- NOT yet run as e2e: cosim / lockstep V paths (their drain_full /
  drain_checkpoint scratch logic is covered at unit level; same threading).
- Replace the fixed `kVScratchGpa` constant with `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base,
  ram_size) = ram_base + ram_size - kVScratchBytes`. The scratch is the top
  `kVScratchBytes` of whatever RAM span is mapped.
- Host stager (`stage_v_to_scratch` / `read_v_from_scratch`) computes the
  offset as `ram_size - kVScratchBytes` (it already receives the span + base).
- `ResumeDriver` / `StateDrain` take the scratch GPA as a required ctor arg
  (no silent default) and pass it to `pb_v_data_sweep`.
- `simulator.hpp` construction sites compute the GPA from
  `platform.main_memory` and pass it down.
- After F1 alone the scratch is the top page of `mem_size` (scheme A: inside
  program RAM, but far above this runtime's 7 MB stack -- already better than
  the mid-RAM 15 MB constant). F2 lifts it above program RAM (scheme D).
- Key files: `verilator/src/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `resume_driver.hpp`,
  `state_drain.hpp`, `program_buffer.hpp` (caller), `simulator.hpp`,
  `resume_from_qemu.hpp`, `handoff_controller.hpp`, `lockstep_controller.hpp`;
  tests `tests/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.test.cpp`, `resume_driver.test.cpp`,
  `state_drain.test.cpp`.
- Deps: none.

### F2. Map one page above --mem-size; scratch sits above program RAM  [state: DONE]
- Verified 2026-06-16: shared ABI gained `HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`
  (= 32*HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX); v_regfile_xfer's `kVScratchBytes` references it.
  Driver helpers `physical_mmap_bytes()` / `max_program_mem_bytes()` (shm.cpp,

message.content: simply explain the hybrid engine's marker mode

content.text:
Marker mode runs the program in two engines and measures only the region you mark.

**The two markers**

You wrap the code you care about with two function calls from `<andes_sim/ROI.h>`:

```c
andes_sim_ROI_begin();   // start measuring here
... the loop you care about ...
andes_sim_ROI_end();     // stop here
```

Each one compiles to a single RISC-V HINT NOP:
- begin -> `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0`
- end -> `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1`

A HINT writes to `x0`, so the result is thrown away. It does nothing to the program. That means the SAME binary still runs normally on real silicon or on any engine - the markers are invisible padding until an engine is told to look for them.

**What hybrid does with them**

```
QEMU (fast, functional)  ---->  vsim (cycle-accurate RTL)
     runs up to begin            runs begin..end, then stops
```

1. QEMU runs the program fast from `_start`. It watches each retired instruction.
2. When QEMU sees the **begin** marker, it freezes and drains all CPU state (registers, CSRs, etc.) into a state file + shared memory.
3. vsim loads that state, then runs the real RTL through your region.
4. When vsim sees the **end** marker, it stops and drains state again.

**The number you get**

`window_cycles` = vsim's `mcycle` at end minus `mcycle` at begin. That is the true cycle cost of just your marked region, measured on the accurate engine - without paying RTL speed for the boring setup code before it.

**Why use it**

The slow accurate engine only runs the small part you marked; the fast engine handles everything else. You get cycle-accurate numbers for a hot loop in a fraction of the time a full RTL run would take.

If you cannot edit the binary to add markers, use `--trigger pc --pc-start S --pc-end E` instead - same idea, but the boundaries are PC addresses or symbol names instead of marker NOPs.

message.content: simply explain the hybrid engine's pc mode

content.text:
PC mode is the same hybrid handoff as marker mode, but you mark the region with **addresses** instead of NOPs.

**How you use it**

```
andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger pc \
  --pc-start <S> --pc-end <E>  your.elf
```

`S` and `E` can be either:
- a symbol name (e.g. `--pc-start main --pc-end loop_done`), or
- a raw address (e.g. `--pc-start 0x100a4`)

Both are required. They are resolved to real PCs once at startup.

**What hybrid does with them**

```
QEMU (fast)  ---->  vsim (cycle)
 runs to PC=S        runs S..E, then stops
```

1. QEMU runs fast from `_start`.
2. When the program counter reaches `S`, QEMU freezes and drains all CPU state.
3. vsim loads that state and runs the real RTL from `S`.
4. When the PC reaches `E`, vsim stops and drains again.

`window_cycles` = vsim `mcycle` at `E` minus `mcycle` at `S` - the cycle cost of the code between those two addresses. In PC mode the marker NOPs are ignored.

**Why it exists**

Use PC mode when you **cannot edit the source** to add `andes_sim_ROI_begin()/end()`. A vendor blob, a prebuilt library, code you do not own - you still pick the exact region by pointing at its addresses.

**The one trade-off vs marker mode**

Markers move with the code: recompile, and the begin/end NOPs stay glued to your loop. PC addresses do not - if you rebuild and the layout shifts, `0x100a4` may no longer be your loop's start. Using **symbol names** instead of raw addresses avoids this, because the symbol is re-resolved each run.

2	# Hot inner-loop detector wrapper (system-mode, baremetal RISC-V).
3	#
4	# Runs a baremetal ELF under qemu-system-<arch> with the hotloops plugin
5	# and prints a sorted table of detected backward branches:
6	#
7	#   iters | start_pc -> end_pc | function:offset
8	#
9	# Usage:
10	#   scripts/hotloops.sh [opts] <elf>
11	#
12	# Options:
13	#   --arch <riscv32|riscv64|auto>   Target arch (default: auto)
14	#   --qemu <path>                   Override qemu-system binary
15	#   --plugin <path>                 Override plugin .so
16	#   --machine <name>                -M <name> (default andes_ae350)
17	#   --cpu <spec>                    -cpu <spec>
18	#                                   (default andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=1024)
19	#   --qemu-config <file>            -readconfig <file> (e.g. AE350 device cfg)
20	#   --cwd <dir>                     chdir before launching QEMU so semihosting
21	#                                   opens (fread of bin/*.bin) resolve
22	#   --qemu-arg <arg>                Append an extra arg to the QEMU command
23	#                                   (repeatable)
24	#   --limit <N>                     Top-N loops to print (default 50)
25	#   --min-iters <N>                 Drop loops with fewer than N iters (default 1)
26	#   --objdump <path>                Override objdump (resolves symbols)
27	#   --addr2line <path>              Override addr2line (resolves source lines)
28	#   --no-source                     Disable source file:line resolution
29	#   --raw                           Print raw plugin output, no formatting
30	#   --optimize-rvv                  Only report loops with at least one RVV
31	#                                   instruction (default: on)
32	#   --no-optimize-rvv               Disable the RVV-only filter
33	#   --llm                           Emit a Markdown report tuned for LLM
34	#                                   consumption: TL;DR + per-loop fact-sheets
35	#                                   with stable IDs, source snippets, RVV
36	#                                   instruction listings, nesting, and direct
37	#                                   callees (default: on).
38	#   --no-llm                        Emit the plain human-readable table.

163	if [[ -n "$OBJDUMP" ]]; then
164	    # Capture FUNC symbols: addr size type name. An ELF visibility token
165	    # (".hidden"/".protected"/".internal") sits between size and name when
166	    # present; drop it so $(NF-1) is always the size (left in place it also
