#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Hot inner-loop detector wrapper (system-mode, baremetal RISC-V).
#
# Runs a baremetal ELF under qemu-system-<arch> with the hotloops plugin
# and prints a sorted table of detected backward branches:
#
#   iters | start_pc -> end_pc | function:offset
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/hotloops.sh [opts] <elf>
#
# Options:
#   --arch <riscv32|riscv64|auto>   Target arch (default: auto)
#   --qemu <path>                   Override qemu-system binary
#   --plugin <path>                 Override plugin .so
#   --machine <name>                -M <name> (default andes_ae350)
#   --cpu <spec>                    -cpu <spec>
#                                   (default andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=1024)
#   --qemu-config <file>            -readconfig <file> (e.g. AE350 device cfg)
#   --cwd <dir>                     chdir before launching QEMU so semihosting
#                                   opens (fread of bin/*.bin) resolve
#   --qemu-arg <arg>                Append an extra arg to the QEMU command
#                                   (repeatable)
#   --limit <N>                     Top-N loops to print (default 50)
#   --min-iters <N>                 Drop loops with fewer than N iters (default 1)
#   --objdump <path>                Override objdump (resolves symbols)
#   --addr2line <path>              Override addr2line (resolves source lines)
#   --no-source                     Disable source file:line resolution
#   --raw                           Print raw plugin output, no formatting
#   --optimize-rvv                  Only report loops with at least one RVV
#                                   instruction (default: on)
#   --no-optimize-rvv               Disable the RVV-only filter
#   --llm                           Emit a Markdown report tuned for LLM
#                                   consumption: TL;DR + per-loop fact-sheets
#                                   with stable IDs, source snippets, RVV
#                                   instruction listings, nesting, and direct
#                                   callees (default: on).
#   --no-llm                        Emit the plain human-readable table.
#   -h | --help                     Show help

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
QEMU_ROOT="$(cd -- "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"

ARCH="auto"
QEMU=""
PLUGIN=""
LIMIT=50
MIN_ITERS=1
OBJDUMP=""
ADDR2LINE=""
NO_SOURCE=0
RAW=0
OPTIMIZE_RVV=1
LLM=1
MACHINE="andes_ae350"
CPU="andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=1024"
QEMU_CONFIG=""
QEMU_CWD=""
EXTRA_QEMU_ARGS=()

usage() { sed -n '2,39p' "$0"; exit 0; }

# --- arg parsing ---
ELF=""
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --arch)        ARCH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --qemu)        QEMU="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --plugin)      PLUGIN="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --machine)     MACHINE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --cpu)         CPU="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --qemu-config) QEMU_CONFIG="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --cwd)         QEMU_CWD="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --qemu-arg)    EXTRA_QEMU_ARGS+=("$2"); shift 2 ;;
        --limit)       LIMIT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --min-iters)   MIN_ITERS="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --objdump)     OBJDUMP="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --addr2line)   ADDR2LINE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --no-source)   NO_SOURCE=1; shift ;;
        --raw)         RAW=1; shift ;;
        --optimize-rvv)    OPTIMIZE_RVV=1; shift ;;
        --no-optimize-rvv) OPTIMIZE_RVV=0; shift ;;
        --llm)             LLM=1; shift ;;
        --no-llm)          LLM=0; shift ;;
        -h|--help)     usage ;;
        -*) echo "unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
        *)
            if [[ -z "$ELF" ]]; then
                ELF="$1"; shift
            else
                echo "error: unexpected positional arg: $1" >&2; exit 2
            fi ;;
    esac
done

[[ -n "$ELF" ]] || { echo "error: ELF path required" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ -f "$ELF" ]] || { echo "error: not found: $ELF" >&2; exit 2; }

# --- arch detection ---
if [[ "$ARCH" == "auto" ]]; then
    file_out="$(file -L -- "$ELF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    case "$file_out" in
        *"ELF 64-bit"*"RISC-V"*)  ARCH=riscv64 ;;
        *"ELF 32-bit"*"RISC-V"*)  ARCH=riscv32 ;;
        *) echo "error: cannot auto-detect arch (not RISC-V?), pass --arch" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
fi

# --- locate qemu + plugin ---
if [[ -z "$QEMU" ]]; then
    QEMU="${QEMU_ROOT}/build/qemu-system-${ARCH}"
fi
[[ -x "$QEMU" ]] || { echo "error: qemu not found/executable: $QEMU" >&2; exit 2; }

if [[ -z "$PLUGIN" ]]; then
    PLUGIN="${QEMU_ROOT}/build/contrib/plugins/libhotloops.so"
fi
[[ -f "$PLUGIN" ]] || { echo "error: plugin not built: $PLUGIN" >&2; exit 2; }

# --- run ---
# Temp files are declared up front so one EXIT trap covers every exit path,
# including the early --raw exit before SYMS/LINES/DISASM are created.
LOG="$(mktemp -t hotloops.XXXXXX.log)"
SYMS="" LINES="" DISASM=""
trap 'rm -f "$LOG" "$SYMS" "$LINES" "$DISASM"' EXIT

QEMU_CMD=("$QEMU"
          -plugin "${PLUGIN},limit=${LIMIT},min_iters=${MIN_ITERS}"
          -d plugin -D "$LOG"
          -M "$MACHINE"
          -cpu "$CPU"
          -nographic -semihosting
          -bios "$ELF")
[[ -n "$QEMU_CONFIG" ]] && QEMU_CMD+=(-readconfig "$QEMU_CONFIG")
[[ ${#EXTRA_QEMU_ARGS[@]} -gt 0 ]] && QEMU_CMD+=("${EXTRA_QEMU_ARGS[@]}")
if [[ -n "$QEMU_CWD" ]]; then
    ( cd "$QEMU_CWD" && "${QEMU_CMD[@]}" ) >/dev/null
else
    "${QEMU_CMD[@]}" >/dev/null
fi

if [[ "$RAW" -eq 1 ]]; then
    cat "$LOG"
    exit 0
fi

# --- symbol table from objdump (best effort) ---
if [[ -z "$OBJDUMP" ]]; then
    for cand in llvm-objdump riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump \
                riscv32-unknown-elf-objdump objdump; do
        if command -v "$cand" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            OBJDUMP="$cand"
            break
        fi
    done
fi

SYMS="$(mktemp -t hotloops_syms.XXXXXX)"
LINES="$(mktemp -t hotloops_lines.XXXXXX)"
DISASM="$(mktemp -t hotloops_disasm.XXXXXX)"
if [[ -n "$OBJDUMP" ]]; then
    # Capture FUNC symbols: addr size type name. An ELF visibility token
    # (".hidden"/".protected"/".internal") sits between size and name when
    # present; drop it so $(NF-1) is always the size (left in place it also
    # kills gawk: strtonum("0x.hidden") parses as a malformed hex float).
    "$OBJDUMP" -t "$ELF" 2>/dev/null \
        | awk '{ sub(/[ \t]\.(hidden|protected|internal)[ \t]/, " ") }
              tolower($0) ~ /[ \t]f[ \t]/ && NF>=5 {
                  addr=strtonum("0x" $1);
                  size=strtonum("0x" $(NF-1));
                  name=$NF;
                  if (size>0) print addr, size, name;
              }' \
        | sort -n -k1,1 > "$SYMS" || true

    # Capture disassembly: each output line is "<hex-pc> <mnemonic> <operands>".
    # Works for both GNU binutils objdump and llvm-objdump. Used by the RVV
    # filter (mnemonic) and --llm mode (operands, callee names).
    if [[ "$OPTIMIZE_RVV" -eq 1 || "$LLM" -eq 1 ]]; then
        "$OBJDUMP" -d --no-show-raw-insn "$ELF" 2>/dev/null \
            | awk '
                /^[ \t]*[0-9a-fA-F]+:[ \t]+[^ \t]+/ {
                    line = $0;
                    sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", line);
                    sub(/[ \t]+$/, "", line);
                    sub(/:[ \t]+/, " ", line);
                    print line;
                }' > "$DISASM" || true
    fi
fi

# --- locate addr2line for source line resolution (DWARF) ---
if [[ "$NO_SOURCE" -eq 0 && -z "$ADDR2LINE" ]]; then
    for cand in llvm-addr2line addr2line \
                riscv64-unknown-elf-addr2line riscv32-unknown-elf-addr2line \
                riscv64-linux-gnu-addr2line; do
        if command -v "$cand" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            ADDR2LINE="$cand"
            break
        fi
    done
fi

# Pre-collect all PCs from the log and batch-resolve to file:line.
# LINES file format: <hex-pc> <file:line>
if [[ "$NO_SOURCE" -eq 0 && -n "$ADDR2LINE" ]]; then
    pcs="$(awk -F',' '/^0x/ {gsub(/[ \t]/,"",$1); gsub(/[ \t]/,"",$2); print $1; print $2}' "$LOG" | sort -u)"
    if [[ -n "$pcs" ]]; then
        # addr2line: -e <elf> reads addrs on stdin, prints file:line.
        # We keep full paths here (no -s) so --llm mode can locate the
        # source file for code snippets; table mode basenames in Python.
        out="$(printf '%s\n' $pcs | "$ADDR2LINE" -e "$ELF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
        paste <(printf '%s\n' $pcs) <(printf '%s\n' "$out") > "$LINES" || true
    fi
fi

# --- format ---
python3 - "$LOG" "$SYMS" "$LINES" "$DISASM" "$LIMIT" "$MIN_ITERS" \
        "$OPTIMIZE_RVV" "$LLM" "$ELF" <<'PY'
import sys, os, re, bisect

log_path     = sys.argv[1]
syms_path    = sys.argv[2]
lines_path   = sys.argv[3]
disasm_path  = sys.argv[4]
limit        = int(sys.argv[5])
min_iters    = int(sys.argv[6])
optimize_rvv = int(sys.argv[7]) == 1
llm_mode     = int(sys.argv[8]) == 1
elf_path     = sys.argv[9]

# --- symbols (FUNC syms): list of (addr, size, name) sorted by addr ---
syms = []
try:
    with open(syms_path) as f:
        for line in f:
            parts = line.split()
            if len(parts) >= 3:
                syms.append((int(parts[0]), int(parts[1]),
                             " ".join(parts[2:])))
except FileNotFoundError:
    pass

def resolve(pc):
    for addr, size, name in syms:
        if addr <= pc < addr + size:
            return f"{name}+0x{pc-addr:x}"
    return "?"

# --- source map: pc -> "path:line" (full path; basename in Python for table) ---
src_map = {}
try:
    with open(lines_path) as f:
        for line in f:
            parts = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t", 1)
            if len(parts) == 2:
                pc_str, src = parts
                src = src.strip()
                if src and not src.startswith("??"):
                    try:
                        src_map[int(pc_str, 16)] = src
                    except ValueError:
                        pass
except FileNotFoundError:
    pass

def src_full(pc):
    return src_map.get(pc, "")

def src_basename(s):
    """Basename the path part of a 'path:line[ (extra)]' string."""
    if not s:
        return ""
    head, sep, tail = s.partition(" ")
    return os.path.basename(head) + (sep + tail if sep else "")

def src_short(pc):
    return src_basename(src_full(pc))

# --- disassembly: pc -> (mnemonic, operands) ---
disasm = {}
try:
    with open(disasm_path) as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.rstrip("\n")
            parts = line.split(None, 2)
            if len(parts) < 2:
                continue
            try:
                pc = int(parts[0], 16)
            except ValueError:
                continue
            mnemonic = parts[1]
            operands = parts[2] if len(parts) >= 3 else ""
            disasm[pc] = (mnemonic, operands)
except FileNotFoundError:
    pass

disasm_pcs = sorted(disasm.keys())

def is_rvv_mnemonic(mn):
    mn = mn.lower()
    return mn.startswith("v") and len(mn) > 1 and mn[1].isalpha()

rvv_pcs = sorted(pc for pc, (mn, _) in disasm.items() if is_rvv_mnemonic(mn))

def rvv_insns_in_range(s, e):
    out = []
    if not rvv_pcs or s > e:
        return out
    i = bisect.bisect_left(rvv_pcs, s)
    while i < len(rvv_pcs) and rvv_pcs[i] <= e:
        pc = rvv_pcs[i]
        mn, ops = disasm[pc]
        out.append((pc, mn, ops))
        i += 1
    return out

CALL_MN = {"jal", "jalr", "c.jal", "c.jalr"}
CALLEE_RE = re.compile(r"<([^>]+)>")

def calls_in_range(s, e):
    out = []
    if not disasm_pcs or s > e:
        return out
    i = bisect.bisect_left(disasm_pcs, s)
    while i < len(disasm_pcs) and disasm_pcs[i] <= e:
        pc = disasm_pcs[i]
        mn, ops = disasm[pc]
        if mn in CALL_MN:
            m = CALLEE_RE.search(ops)
            target = m.group(1) if m else "(indirect)"
            out.append((pc, mn, target))
        i += 1
    return out

def parse_file_line(s):
    """'path:42' or 'path:42 (discriminator 1)' -> (path, 42)."""
    if not s or s.startswith("??"):
        return None, None
    m = re.match(r"^(.+?):(\d+)(?::\d+)?(?:\s|$)", s)
    if not m:
        return None, None
    return m.group(1), int(m.group(2))

def read_source_line(path, lineno):
    if not path or not os.path.isfile(path):
        return None
    try:
        with open(path, errors="replace") as f:
            for i, line in enumerate(f, 1):
                if i == lineno:
                    return line.rstrip()
    except OSError:
        return None
    return None

# --- raw rows from plugin ---
rows = []
with open(log_path) as f:
    for line in f:
        m = re.match(r"\s*(0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)\s*,\s*(0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)\s*,\s*(\d+)",
                     line)
        if m:
            rows.append((int(m.group(1), 16),
                         int(m.group(2), 16),
                         int(m.group(3))))

if not rows:
    sys.stderr.write("hotloops: no backward edges observed\n")
    sys.exit(0)

total_iters_all = sum(r[2] for r in rows)

rows = [r for r in rows if r[2] >= min_iters]
if optimize_rvv:
    rows = [r for r in rows if rvv_insns_in_range(r[0], r[1])]
rows.sort(key=lambda r: -r[2])
rows = rows[:limit]

if not rows:
    msg = f"hotloops: no loops with iters >= {min_iters}"
    if optimize_rvv:
        msg += " containing RVV instructions"
    sys.stderr.write(msg + "\n")
    sys.exit(0)

# --- Loop objects + nesting (PC-range containment) ---
class Loop:
    __slots__ = ("id", "start", "end", "iters", "parent", "children")
    def __init__(self, idx, s, e, c):
        self.id = f"L{idx}"
        self.start = s
        self.end = e
        self.iters = c
        self.parent = None
        self.children = []

loops = [Loop(i + 1, s, e, c) for i, (s, e, c) in enumerate(rows)]

for loop in loops:
    best = None
    best_size = None
    for cand in loops:
        if cand is loop:
            continue
        if cand.start <= loop.start and loop.end <= cand.end:
            if cand.start == loop.start and cand.end == loop.end:
                continue  # identical range, ambiguous - skip
            sz = cand.end - cand.start
            if best is None or sz < best_size:
                best = cand
                best_size = sz
    loop.parent = best

for loop in loops:
    if loop.parent is not None:
        loop.parent.children.append(loop)

def func_of(pc):
    for addr, size, name in syms:
        if addr <= pc < addr + size:
            return addr, size, name
    return None

def measure_window(loop):
    """A ready hybrid pc window covering EVERY iteration of the loop:
    its enclosing function's [entry, ret). The loop's own pc_range is not
    usable (one-shot pc triggers fire on the first hit, so header..tail
    spans a single iteration). None when no sized FUNC symbol encloses
    the whole loop or the function has zero/multiple `ret`s (tail-called
    or multi-epilogue) - then the boundaries need a human/agent choice."""
    fn = func_of(loop.start)
    if fn is None:
        return None
    addr, size, name = fn
    if not (addr <= loop.end < addr + size):
        return None
    def is_ret(mn, ops):
        # llvm-objdump aliases to `ret`; GNU/Andes objdump may print the
        # compressed form unaliased as `c.jr ra` (or `jr ra`).
        return mn == "ret" or (mn in ("jr", "c.jr")
                               and ops.split(",")[0].strip() == "ra")
    rets = []
    i = bisect.bisect_left(disasm_pcs, addr)
    while i < len(disasm_pcs) and disasm_pcs[i] < addr + size:
        pc = disasm_pcs[i]
        if is_ret(*disasm[pc]):
            rets.append(pc)
        i += 1
    if len(rets) != 1:
        return None
    return addr, rets[0], name

def measure_loop_window(loop):
    """First-pass window for the loop itself: [header, fall-through of the
    backward branch). The window drains the FIRST time the branch is not
    taken, so a re-entered loop (e.g. the inner loop of a nest, restarted
    by every outer iteration) measures only its first complete pass. The
    fall-through PC is the next instruction in the disassembly (exact for
    compressed branches; never a +4 guess)."""
    i = bisect.bisect_right(disasm_pcs, loop.end)
    if i >= len(disasm_pcs):
        return None
    ft = disasm_pcs[i]
    if ft - loop.end > 4:  # not linear fall-through (disassembly gap)
        return None
    return loop.start, ft

# ============================================================
# --- LLM mode: Markdown report with TL;DR + per-loop blocks ---
# ============================================================
if llm_mode:
    def pct(n):
        return (100.0 * n / total_iters_all) if total_iters_all else 0.0

    def render_tldr(top):
        rvv_list = rvv_insns_in_range(top.start, top.end)
        if rvv_list:
            uniq = list(dict.fromkeys(mn for _, mn, _ in rvv_list))
            rvv_str = "RVV (" + ", ".join(uniq[:3])
            if len(uniq) > 3:
                rvv_str += f", +{len(uniq) - 3} more"
            rvv_str += ")"
        else:
            rvv_str = "scalar"
        fn = resolve(top.start).split("+")[0]
        src_s = src_short(top.start) or "?"
        if top.parent is None:
            nest_str = "top-level (no parent loop)"
        else:
            nest_str = f"nested inside {top.parent.id}"
        if top.children:
            cs = ", ".join(c.id for c in top.children)
            child_str = (f"and contains {len(top.children)} inner loop(s): "
                         f"{cs}")
        else:
            child_str = "and contains no inner loop"
        out = (f"Hottest loop is {top.id} in `{fn}` ({src_s}), "
               f"{top.iters} iters = {pct(top.iters):.1f}% of total. "
               f"Body is {rvv_str}. It is {nest_str}, {child_str}.")
        mw = measure_window(top)
        if mw:
            s, e, name = mw
            out += (f" Measure all of `{name}` with: "
                    f"--pc-start 0x{s:x} --pc-end 0x{e:x}.")
        return out

    print("# Hotloops Report")
    print(f"target:           {os.path.basename(elf_path)}")
    print(f"total_iters:      {total_iters_all}")
    print(f"reported_loops:   {len(loops)}")
    print(f"min_iters:        {min_iters}")
    print(f"rvv_filter:       {'on' if optimize_rvv else 'off'}")
    print()
    print("## TL;DR")
    print(render_tldr(loops[0]))
    print()
    print("## Loops")
    for idx, loop in enumerate(loops):
        tag = " [hottest]" if idx == 0 else ""
        print()
        print(f"### {loop.id}{tag}  ({pct(loop.iters):.1f}% of total)")
        print(f"iters:        {loop.iters}")
        size = loop.end - loop.start
        print(f"pc_range:     0x{loop.start:x} .. 0x{loop.end:x}  "
              f"(size: {size} B)")
        print(f"function:     {resolve(loop.start)} -> {resolve(loop.end)}")
        mw = measure_window(loop)
        if mw:
            s, e, name = mw
            print(f"measure:      --pc-start 0x{s:x} --pc-end 0x{e:x}"
                  f"  (all of {name}: entry -> ret)")
        else:
            print(f"measure:      -  (no single-ret enclosing function;"
                  f" pick boundaries manually)")
        ml = measure_loop_window(loop)
        if ml:
            s, e = ml
            print(f"measure_loop: --pc-start 0x{s:x} --pc-end 0x{e:x}"
                  f"  (this loop only, first pass: header -> fall-through)")
        src_s = src_full(loop.start)
        src_e = src_full(loop.end)
        if src_s and src_e and src_s == src_e:
            print(f"source:       {src_basename(src_s)}")
        else:
            print(f"source:       {src_basename(src_s) or '?'}"
                  f" -> {src_basename(src_e) or '?'}")
        path, lineno = parse_file_line(src_s)
        snippet = read_source_line(path, lineno) if path and lineno else None
        if snippet:
            snippet = snippet.strip()
            if len(snippet) > 200:
                snippet = snippet[:197] + "..."
            print(f"code:         {snippet}")
        rvv_list = rvv_insns_in_range(loop.start, loop.end)
        if rvv_list:
            print(f"rvv:          yes ({len(rvv_list)} insn"
                  f"{'s' if len(rvv_list) != 1 else ''})")
            print(f"rvv_insns:")
            for pc, mn, ops in rvv_list[:8]:
                print(f"  - 0x{pc:x}  {mn:<10s} {ops}")
            if len(rvv_list) > 8:
                print(f"  - ... ({len(rvv_list) - 8} more)")
        else:
            print(f"rvv:          no")
        print(f"parent:       {loop.parent.id if loop.parent else '-'}")
        if loop.children:
            cs = ", ".join(c.id for c in loop.children)
            print(f"children:     [{cs}]")
        else:
            print(f"children:     []")
        callees = calls_in_range(loop.start, loop.end)
        if callees:
            print(f"calls:")
            for pc, mn, target in callees[:8]:
                print(f"  - 0x{pc:x}  {mn} -> {target}")
            if len(callees) > 8:
                print(f"  - ... ({len(callees) - 8} more)")
        else:
            print(f"calls:        []")
    sys.exit(0)

# ============================================================
# --- table mode (default, human-readable) ---
# ============================================================
hdr = f"# hot loops (iters >= {min_iters}"
if optimize_rvv:
    hdr += ", RVV-only"
hdr += f"), sorted desc, top {len(rows)}"
print(hdr)

have_src = bool(src_map)

def srcpair(s, e):
    a, b = src_short(s), src_short(e)
    if a and b and a == b:
        return a
    return f"{a or '?'} -> {b or '?'}"

w_iter = max(len("iters"), max(len(str(r[2])) for r in rows))
w_pc = 18  # 0x + 16 hex
w_sym = max(len("location"),
            max(len(f"{resolve(r[0])} -> {resolve(r[1])}") for r in rows))

sep = w_iter + 3 + w_pc + 4 + w_pc + 3 + w_sym
if have_src:
    w_src = max(len("source"), max(len(srcpair(r[0], r[1])) for r in rows))
    sep += 3 + w_src
    print(f"{'iters':>{w_iter}} | {'start_pc':<{w_pc}} -> "
          f"{'end_pc':<{w_pc}} | {'location':<{w_sym}} | source")
else:
    print(f"{'iters':>{w_iter}} | {'start_pc':<{w_pc}} -> "
          f"{'end_pc':<{w_pc}} | location")
print("-" * sep)
for s, e, c in rows:
    loc = f"{resolve(s)} -> {resolve(e)}"
    row = f"{c:>{w_iter}} | 0x{s:016x} -> 0x{e:016x} | "
    row += f"{loc:<{w_sym}} | {srcpair(s, e)}" if have_src else loc
    print(row)

1	# hotloops - hot inner-loop detector
2	
3	Detects the hottest loops in a baremetal RISC-V ELF by observing backward
4	translation-block transitions in `qemu-system-<arch>`. For each detected
5	loop you get the loop header PC, the backward-branch PC, and the iteration
6	count. With DWARF, you also get the source `file:line`. With objdump
7	present, you get RVV-only filtering and per-loop disassembly context.
8	
9	Two parts ship together:
10	
11	- `contrib/plugins/hotloops.c` - QEMU TCG plugin that records edges.
12	- `scripts/hotloops.sh` - wrapper that runs the plugin and formats output.
13	
14	## Usage
15	
16	```
17	scripts/hotloops.sh [options] <elf>
18	```
19	
20	The wrapper launches `qemu-system-<arch>` with `-bios <elf>` on a baremetal
21	machine (default `andes_ae350`) and a vector-capable CPU (default
22	`andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=1024`). Override per the options below
23	for other targets.
24	
25	### Options
26	
27	| Flag                | Default            | Description                                                    |
28	|---------------------|--------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
29	| `--arch <a>`        | auto               | Target arch: `riscv32`, `riscv64`, or `auto` (from `file`).    |
30	| `--qemu <path>`     | auto               | Override the `qemu-system-<arch>` binary.                      |
31	| `--plugin <path>`   | auto               | Override the plugin `.so`.                                     |
32	| `--machine <name>`  | `andes_ae350`      | `-M <name>` passed to QEMU.                                    |
33	| `--cpu <spec>`      | `andes-ax45mpv,...`| `-cpu <spec>` passed to QEMU. Default enables RVV 1.0 vlen=1024.|
34	| `--qemu-config <f>` | -                  | `-readconfig <file>` (e.g. AE350 device cfg).                  |
35	| `--cwd <dir>`       | -                  | `chdir` before launching QEMU (so semihosting `fread` of `bin/*.bin` resolves). |
36	| `--qemu-arg <arg>`  | -                  | Extra arg appended to the QEMU command. Repeatable.            |
37	| `--limit <N>`       | 50                 | Print at most N loops.                                         |
38	| `--min-iters <N>`   | 1                  | Drop loops with fewer than N iterations (hot-loop threshold).  |
39	| `--objdump <path>`  | auto               | Override objdump (for `function+offset` and disassembly).      |
40	| `--addr2line <path>`| auto               | Override addr2line (for source-line resolution).               |
41	| `--no-source`       | off                | Skip source resolution even if DWARF is present.               |
42	| `--raw`             | off                | Print raw plugin output (CSV-ish), no formatting.              |
43	| `--optimize-rvv`    | on                 | Only report loops that contain at least one RVV instruction.   |
44	| `--no-optimize-rvv` | off                | Disable the RVV-only filter; report all loops.                 |
45	| `--llm`             | on                 | Emit a Markdown report tuned for LLM consumption (see below).  |
46	| `--no-llm`          | off                | Emit the plain human-readable table instead of the LLM report. |
47	
48	### Build prerequisites
49	
50	The plugin lives in `contrib/plugins/`. Build once:
51	
52	```
53	ninja -C build contrib-plugins
54	```
55	
56	It is incremental on subsequent edits to `hotloops.c`. The QEMU binaries
57	themselves (`qemu-system-riscv64`, `qemu-system-riscv32`) do **not** need
58	to be rebuilt.
59	
60	## How it detects a loop
61	
62	For every translated block, the plugin remembers the PC of its last
63	instruction. When the next-executed block starts at a PC `<=` that
64	remembered PC, the transition is a backward edge - i.e. a loop iteration.
65	The pair `(header_pc, tail_pc)` is the key; the count is the number of
66	iterations.
67	
68	This catches every loop a real backward branch closes (for/while/do-while,
69	goto, manually unrolled tails, etc.) without needing to model branch
70	semantics.
71	
72	Caveat: each iteration counted is one *taken* backward branch. A loop
73	that runs N times has N-1 taken backward branches plus one fall-through
74	on exit, so the reported count is N-1 per call to the enclosing function.
75	
76	## Output modes
77	
78	Three output modes, in order of layered post-processing:
79	
80	1. `--llm` (default on) - Markdown report tuned for LLM consumption.
81	2. `--no-llm` - plain human-readable table.
82	3. `--raw` - unformatted plugin output (overrides the above).
83	
84	### LLM report (default)
85	
86	The wrapper emits a single Markdown document structured so an LLM (or a
87	reader skimming top-down) can answer "what is the hottest loop?" from the
88	first paragraph, then drill down via stable IDs.
89	
90	Layout:
91	
92	- Header block: `target`, `total_iters`, `reported_loops`, `min_iters`,
93	  `rvv_filter`.
94	- `## TL;DR` paragraph naming the hottest loop, its function and source
95	  line, percentage of total iterations, RVV vs scalar (with the top-K
96	  unique vector mnemonics seen), nesting status, and (when derivable)
97	  the ready measure window for the hottest loop.
98	- One `### L<N>` fact-sheet per reported loop (sorted by iters desc):
99	  - `iters` and `pc_range` (`0xstart .. 0xend  (size: N B)`).
100	  - `function` (`fn+0xoff -> fn+0xoff`).
101	  - `measure` - a ready hybrid pc window covering EVERY iteration of the
102	    loop: `--pc-start 0x<entry> --pc-end 0x<ret>` of the enclosing
103	    function. (The loop's own `pc_range` is NOT a usable window: one-shot
104	    pc triggers fire on the first hit, so header..tail spans a single
105	    iteration.) Shown as `-` when no sized FUNC symbol encloses the loop
106	    or the function has zero/multiple `ret`s (tail-called or
107	    multi-epilogue) - pick the boundaries manually then.
108	  - `measure_loop` - a ready window for the loop alone:
109	    `--pc-start 0x<header> --pc-end 0x<fall-through>` (the instruction
110	    after the backward branch, taken from the disassembly - exact for
111	    compressed branches). It drains the FIRST time the loop exits, so a
112	    re-entered loop (the inner loop of a nest) measures its first
113	    complete pass only - multiply by the trip count of the enclosing
114	    loop(s) to extrapolate. Omitted when the disassembly has no linear
115	    fall-through after the branch.
116	  - `source` (`file:line` or `file:line -> file:line` if the header and
117	    tail map to different lines).
118	  - `code` - inline best-effort source snippet read from the path stored
119	    in DWARF.
120	  - `rvv` summary plus `rvv_insns:` listing (capped at 8) with each
121	    `0xpc  mnemonic operands`.
122	  - `parent` / `children` - stable IDs of containing / contained loops.
123	    Inferred from PC-range containment, so this captures only
124	    same-function nesting.
125	  - `calls` - direct callees inside the loop body (`jal`/`jalr` with a
126	    statically known target via the `<name>` annotation). Indirect calls
127	    show as `(indirect)`.
128	
129	The TL;DR is templated from the same data fields the per-loop blocks use;
130	no LLM call is made by the script itself.
131	
132	Limitations:
133	
134	- Same-function nesting only. A caller's hot loop that calls a callee
135	  containing its own hot loop will show as two unrelated loops; follow
136	  `calls:` to bridge.
137	- `code:` snippets require the source file to be reachable at the
138	  absolute path stored in DWARF. Cross-compiled or relocated builds may
139	  fall back to just `file:line`.
140	- The RVV filter is mnemonic-based: any insn whose mnemonic begins with
141	  `v<alpha>` (e.g. `vsetvli`, `vle32.v`, `vadd.vv`, `vmul.vv`). Standard
142	  scalar RISC-V has no such mnemonic, so this is exact in practice.
143	
144	### Table mode (`--no-llm`)
145	
146	Header line, then a fixed-width table sorted by `iters` descending:
147	
148	```
149	# hot loops (iters >= <threshold>[, RVV-only]), sorted desc, top <K>
150	iters | start_pc           -> end_pc             | location              | source
151	-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
152	<n>   | 0x<16-hex>         -> 0x<16-hex>         | <fn>+0x<o> -> <fn>+0x<o> | file:line -> file:line
153	...
154	```
155	
156	Columns:
157	
158	- `iters`     - taken backward-branch count (sorted desc).
159	- `start_pc`  - PC of the loop header (the branch target).
160	- `end_pc`    - PC of the backward branch (the loop tail).
161	- `location`  - `function+offset -> function+offset` from the ELF symbol
162	                table. Shows `?` if the address is not inside any sized
163	                FUNC symbol.
164	- `source`    - `file:line -> file:line` from DWARF (basenamed).
165	                Collapsed to a single `file:line` when both ends map to
166	                the same source line. Only present when the ELF has debug
167	                info and `--no-source` is not set.
168	
169	### Raw mode (`--raw`)
170	
171	Bypasses both the LLM report and the table, printing the unformatted
172	plugin output:
173	
174	```
175	hotloops: <distinct> distinct backward edges, <hot> hot (>= <thr> iters), sorted by iterations desc
176	start_pc, end_pc, iterations
177	0x..., 0x..., <n>
178	...
179	```
180	
181	Stable across releases - useful for piping into another tool.
182	
183	## Example
184	
185	A doubly-nested loop with an RVV inner body:
186	
187	```c
188	/* hotloops_demo.c - baremetal entry */
189	#include <stdint.h>
190	
191	__attribute__((noinline))
192	static int dot_rvv(const int *a, const int *b, int n) {
193	    int s = 0;
194	    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += a[i] * b[i];   /* line 6, vectorized */
195	    return s;
196	}
197	
198	void main(void) {
199	    static int a[64], b[64];
200	    for (int i = 0; i < 64; i++) { a[i] = i; b[i] = 64 - i; }
201	    long total = 0;
202	    for (int outer = 0; outer < 500; outer++)
203	        total += dot_rvv(a, b, 64);                  /* 64 * 500 inner iters */
204	    (void)total;
205	}
206	```
207	
208	Build for AE350 with the Andes RISC-V toolchain (or any baremetal
209	RVV-capable toolchain), then run:
210	
211	```
212	$ scripts/hotloops.sh --min-iters 100 --limit 5 build/hotloops_demo.elf
213	```
214	
215	LLM-mode output (the default) looks like:
216	
217	```markdown
218	# Hotloops Report
219	target:           hotloops_demo.elf
220	total_iters:      32000
221	reported_loops:   1
222	min_iters:        100
223	rvv_filter:       on
224	
225	## TL;DR
226	Hottest loop is L1 in `dot_rvv` (hotloops_demo.c:6), 31500 iters = 98.4% of
227	total. Body is RVV (vsetvli, vle32.v, vmul.vv, +1 more). It is top-level
228	(no parent loop), and contains no inner loop. Measure all of `dot_rvv`
229	with: --pc-start 0x800001f0 --pc-end 0x80000220.
230	
231	## Loops
232	
233	### L1 [hottest]  (98.4% of total)
234	iters:        31500
235	pc_range:     0x80000200 .. 0x80000218  (size: 24 B)
236	function:     dot_rvv+0x10 -> dot_rvv+0x28
237	measure:      --pc-start 0x800001f0 --pc-end 0x80000220  (all of dot_rvv: entry -> ret)
238	measure_loop: --pc-start 0x80000200 --pc-end 0x8000021c  (this loop only, first pass: header -> fall-through)
239	source:       hotloops_demo.c:6
240	code:         for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += a[i] * b[i];   /* line 6, vectorized */
241	rvv:          yes (4 insns)
242	rvv_insns:
243	  - 0x80000200  vsetvli    t0,a2,e32,m1,ta,ma
244	  - 0x80000208  vle32.v    v1,(a0)
245	  - 0x8000020c  vmul.vv    v2,v1,v3
246	  - 0x80000210  vadd.vv    v4,v4,v2
247	parent:       -
248	children:     []
249	calls:        []
250	```
251	
252	Reading the report:
253	
254	- The TL;DR alone identifies the hot path: `dot_rvv` line 6, 98.4% of all
255	  taken backward branches, RVV-vectorized.
256	- The `measure:` flags can be pasted straight into
257	  `andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger pc ...` to get the cycle count
258	  of the whole hot function on the RTL - no objdump step needed.
259	- `measure_loop:` is the same idea for the loop alone. Here `dot_rvv` is
260	  called 500 times, so the window covers the first call's full loop
261	  (64 elements); multiply by 500 for the whole-run estimate.

file.content:
# hotloops - hot inner-loop detector

Detects the hottest loops in a baremetal RISC-V ELF by observing backward
translation-block transitions in `qemu-system-<arch>`. For each detected
loop you get the loop header PC, the backward-branch PC, and the iteration
count. With DWARF, you also get the source `file:line`. With objdump
present, you get RVV-only filtering and per-loop disassembly context.

Two parts ship together:

- `contrib/plugins/hotloops.c` - QEMU TCG plugin that records edges.
- `scripts/hotloops.sh` - wrapper that runs the plugin and formats output.

## Usage

```
scripts/hotloops.sh [options] <elf>
```

The wrapper launches `qemu-system-<arch>` with `-bios <elf>` on a baremetal
machine (default `andes_ae350`) and a vector-capable CPU (default
`andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=1024`). Override per the options below
for other targets.

### Options

| Flag                | Default            | Description                                                    |
|---------------------|--------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| `--arch <a>`        | auto               | Target arch: `riscv32`, `riscv64`, or `auto` (from `file`).    |
| `--qemu <path>`     | auto               | Override the `qemu-system-<arch>` binary.                      |
| `--plugin <path>`   | auto               | Override the plugin `.so`.                                     |
| `--machine <name>`  | `andes_ae350`      | `-M <name>` passed to QEMU.                                    |
| `--cpu <spec>`      | `andes-ax45mpv,...`| `-cpu <spec>` passed to QEMU. Default enables RVV 1.0 vlen=1024.|
| `--qemu-config <f>` | -                  | `-readconfig <file>` (e.g. AE350 device cfg).                  |
| `--cwd <dir>`       | -                  | `chdir` before launching QEMU (so semihosting `fread` of `bin/*.bin` resolves). |
| `--qemu-arg <arg>`  | -                  | Extra arg appended to the QEMU command. Repeatable.            |
| `--limit <N>`       | 50                 | Print at most N loops.                                         |
| `--min-iters <N>`   | 1                  | Drop loops with fewer than N iterations (hot-loop threshold).  |
| `--objdump <path>`  | auto               | Override objdump (for `function+offset` and disassembly).      |
| `--addr2line <path>`| auto               | Override addr2line (for source-line resolution).               |
| `--no-source`       | off                | Skip source resolution even if DWARF is present.               |
| `--raw`             | off                | Print raw plugin output (CSV-ish), no formatting.              |
| `--optimize-rvv`    | on                 | Only report loops that contain at least one RVV instruction.   |
| `--no-optimize-rvv` | off                | Disable the RVV-only filter; report all loops.                 |
| `--llm`             | on                 | Emit a Markdown report tuned for LLM consumption (see below).  |
| `--no-llm`          | off                | Emit the plain human-readable table instead of the LLM report. |

### Build prerequisites

The plugin lives in `contrib/plugins/`. Build once:

```
ninja -C build contrib-plugins
```

It is incremental on subsequent edits to `hotloops.c`. The QEMU binaries
themselves (`qemu-system-riscv64`, `qemu-system-riscv32`) do **not** need
to be rebuilt.

## How it detects a loop

For every translated block, the plugin remembers the PC of its last
instruction. When the next-executed block starts at a PC `<=` that
remembered PC, the transition is a backward edge - i.e. a loop iteration.
The pair `(header_pc, tail_pc)` is the key; the count is the number of
iterations.

This catches every loop a real backward branch closes (for/while/do-while,
goto, manually unrolled tails, etc.) without needing to model branch
semantics.

Caveat: each iteration counted is one *taken* backward branch. A loop
that runs N times has N-1 taken backward branches plus one fall-through
on exit, so the reported count is N-1 per call to the enclosing function.

## Output modes

Three output modes, in order of layered post-processing:

1. `--llm` (default on) - Markdown report tuned for LLM consumption.
2. `--no-llm` - plain human-readable table.
3. `--raw` - unformatted plugin output (overrides the above).

### LLM report (default)

The wrapper emits a single Markdown document structured so an LLM (or a
reader skimming top-down) can answer "what is the hottest loop?" from the
first paragraph, then drill down via stable IDs.

Layout:

- Header block: `target`, `total_iters`, `reported_loops`, `min_iters`,
  `rvv_filter`.
- `## TL;DR` paragraph naming the hottest loop, its function and source
  line, percentage of total iterations, RVV vs scalar (with the top-K
  unique vector mnemonics seen), nesting status, and (when derivable)
  the ready measure window for the hottest loop.
- One `### L<N>` fact-sheet per reported loop (sorted by iters desc):
  - `iters` and `pc_range` (`0xstart .. 0xend  (size: N B)`).
  - `function` (`fn+0xoff -> fn+0xoff`).
  - `measure` - a ready hybrid pc window covering EVERY iteration of the
    loop: `--pc-start 0x<entry> --pc-end 0x<ret>` of the enclosing
    function. (The loop's own `pc_range` is NOT a usable window: one-shot
    pc triggers fire on the first hit, so header..tail spans a single
    iteration.) Shown as `-` when no sized FUNC symbol encloses the loop
    or the function has zero/multiple `ret`s (tail-called or
    multi-epilogue) - pick the boundaries manually then.
  - `measure_loop` - a ready window for the loop alone:
    `--pc-start 0x<header> --pc-end 0x<fall-through>` (the instruction
    after the backward branch, taken from the disassembly - exact for
    compressed branches). It drains the FIRST time the loop exits, so a
    re-entered loop (the inner loop of a nest) measures its first
    complete pass only - multiply by the trip count of the enclosing
    loop(s) to extrapolate. Omitted when the disassembly has no linear
    fall-through after the branch.
  - `source` (`file:line` or `file:line -> file:line` if the header and
    tail map to different lines).
  - `code` - inline best-effort source snippet read from the path stored
    in DWARF.
  - `rvv` summary plus `rvv_insns:` listing (capped at 8) with each
    `0xpc  mnemonic operands`.
  - `parent` / `children` - stable IDs of containing / contained loops.
    Inferred from PC-range containment, so this captures only
    same-function nesting.
  - `calls` - direct callees inside the loop body (`jal`/`jalr` with a
    statically known target via the `<name>` annotation). Indirect calls
    show as `(indirect)`.

The TL;DR is templated from the same data fields the per-loop blocks use;
no LLM call is made by the script itself.

Limitations:

- Same-function nesting only. A caller's hot loop that calls a callee
  containing its own hot loop will show as two unrelated loops; follow
  `calls:` to bridge.
- `code:` snippets require the source file to be reachable at the
  absolute path stored in DWARF. Cross-compiled or relocated builds may
  fall back to just `file:line`.
- The RVV filter is mnemonic-based: any insn whose mnemonic begins with
  `v<alpha>` (e.g. `vsetvli`, `vle32.v`, `vadd.vv`, `vmul.vv`). Standard
  scalar RISC-V has no such mnemonic, so this is exact in practice.

### Table mode (`--no-llm`)

Header line, then a fixed-width table sorted by `iters` descending:

```
# hot loops (iters >= <threshold>[, RVV-only]), sorted desc, top <K>
iters | start_pc           -> end_pc             | location              | source
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
<n>   | 0x<16-hex>         -> 0x<16-hex>         | <fn>+0x<o> -> <fn>+0x<o> | file:line -> file:line
...
```

Columns:

- `iters`     - taken backward-branch count (sorted desc).
- `start_pc`  - PC of the loop header (the branch target).
- `end_pc`    - PC of the backward branch (the loop tail).
- `location`  - `function+offset -> function+offset` from the ELF symbol
                table. Shows `?` if the address is not inside any sized
                FUNC symbol.
- `source`    - `file:line -> file:line` from DWARF (basenamed).
                Collapsed to a single `file:line` when both ends map to
                the same source line. Only present when the ELF has debug
                info and `--no-source` is not set.

### Raw mode (`--raw`)

Bypasses both the LLM report and the table, printing the unformatted
plugin output:

```
hotloops: <distinct> distinct backward edges, <hot> hot (>= <thr> iters), sorted by iterations desc
start_pc, end_pc, iterations
0x..., 0x..., <n>
...
```

Stable across releases - useful for piping into another tool.

## Example

A doubly-nested loop with an RVV inner body:

```c
/* hotloops_demo.c - baremetal entry */
#include <stdint.h>

__attribute__((noinline))
static int dot_rvv(const int *a, const int *b, int n) {
    int s = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += a[i] * b[i];   /* line 6, vectorized */
    return s;
}

void main(void) {
    static int a[64], b[64];
    for (int i = 0; i < 64; i++) { a[i] = i; b[i] = 64 - i; }
    long total = 0;
    for (int outer = 0; outer < 500; outer++)
        total += dot_rvv(a, b, 64);                  /* 64 * 500 inner iters */
    (void)total;
}
```

Build for AE350 with the Andes RISC-V toolchain (or any baremetal
RVV-capable toolchain), then run:

```
$ scripts/hotloops.sh --min-iters 100 --limit 5 build/hotloops_demo.elf
```

LLM-mode output (the default) looks like:

```markdown
# Hotloops Report
target:           hotloops_demo.elf
total_iters:      32000
reported_loops:   1
min_iters:        100
rvv_filter:       on

## TL;DR
Hottest loop is L1 in `dot_rvv` (hotloops_demo.c:6), 31500 iters = 98.4% of
total. Body is RVV (vsetvli, vle32.v, vmul.vv, +1 more). It is top-level
(no parent loop), and contains no inner loop. Measure all of `dot_rvv`
with: --pc-start 0x800001f0 --pc-end 0x80000220.

## Loops

### L1 [hottest]  (98.4% of total)
iters:        31500
pc_range:     0x80000200 .. 0x80000218  (size: 24 B)
function:     dot_rvv+0x10 -> dot_rvv+0x28
measure:      --pc-start 0x800001f0 --pc-end 0x80000220  (all of dot_rvv: entry -> ret)
measure_loop: --pc-start 0x80000200 --pc-end 0x8000021c  (this loop only, first pass: header -> fall-through)
source:       hotloops_demo.c:6
code:         for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += a[i] * b[i];   /* line 6, vectorized */
rvv:          yes (4 insns)
rvv_insns:
  - 0x80000200  vsetvli    t0,a2,e32,m1,ta,ma
  - 0x80000208  vle32.v    v1,(a0)
  - 0x8000020c  vmul.vv    v2,v1,v3
  - 0x80000210  vadd.vv    v4,v4,v2
parent:       -
children:     []
calls:        []
```

Reading the report:

- The TL;DR alone identifies the hot path: `dot_rvv` line 6, 98.4% of all
  taken backward branches, RVV-vectorized.
- The `measure:` flags can be pasted straight into
  `andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger pc ...` to get the cycle count
  of the whole hot function on the RTL - no objdump step needed.
- `measure_loop:` is the same idea for the loop alone. Here `dot_rvv` is
  called 500 times, so the window covers the first call's full loop
  (64 elements); multiply by 500 for the whole-run estimate.
- `iters = 31500` is close to the expected `64 * 500 = 32000`; the missing
  500 are the per-call exits (last iter of `dot_rvv` falls through instead
  of branching back).
- The 500-iter outer loop in `main` was filtered out by `--min-iters 100`.
  It would also have been filtered by the default RVV-only filter since
  `main`'s body is scalar (drop with `--no-optimize-rvv` to see scalar
  loops too).

For piping into a different tool, use `--raw`:

```
$ scripts/hotloops.sh --raw build/hotloops_demo.elf | head
hotloops: 1 distinct backward edges, 1 hot (>= 1 iters), sorted by iterations desc
start_pc, end_pc, iterations
0x0000000080000200, 0x0000000080000218, 31500
```

## Tips

- Strip rarely-interesting startup loops by raising `--min-iters` to a
  value above your background noise floor (e.g. `--min-iters 1000` for a
  workload that runs your hot path millions of times).
- For a very short workload, lower `--min-iters` and raise `--limit`
  to see the full distribution.
- Default settings filter to RVV-containing loops only; pair with
  `--no-optimize-rvv` if you also want to see the scalar hot spots
  (e.g. an outer driver loop wrapping a vectorized kernel).
- For LLM consumption, pipe the default output straight into your prompt
  - the TL;DR is in the first ~10 lines and the per-loop blocks are
  cross-referenceable by their `L<N>` IDs.
- `--raw` is the stable interface for downstream tooling.

lastPrompt: explain the hotloop script and how to use with pc trigger mode

content.text:
hotloops finds your program's hottest loops, then hands you the exact `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` flags to feed `--trigger pc`. It is the "where should I measure?" step before the "measure it" step.

## What the script does

`QEMU/scripts/hotloops.sh <elf>` runs your ELF under `qemu-system-riscv64` with the `hotloops.c` TCG plugin. The plugin watches every block transition; when execution jumps **backward** (a loop closing), it records `(header_pc, tail_pc)` and counts the iterations. No source instrumentation, no markers - it just observes branches.

Then the wrapper decorates the raw counts using your toolchain:
- `objdump` -> `function+offset` and per-loop disassembly (also the RVV filter)
- `addr2line` -> `file:line` (needs the ELF built with `-g`)

By default it prints an LLM-friendly Markdown report: a TL;DR naming the hottest loop, then one fact-sheet per loop.

## The key output: a ready pc window

For each loop the report prints two pre-computed windows you paste straight into hybrid:

- `measure:` = the **whole enclosing function**, entry -> its single `ret`. This covers EVERY iteration of the loop.
- `measure_loop:` = the **loop alone**, header -> the instruction right after the backward branch (first pass only).

Why two? A one-shot PC trigger fires the first time the PC is hit. So the loop's own `header..tail` range would only span one iteration. `measure:` (function entry -> ret) is the safe window for total cost; `measure_loop:` measures one pass and you multiply by the trip count.

## The workflow with pc trigger mode

```sh
# 1. find the hot loop (note: pass the repo's built qemu + plugin paths)
QEMU/scripts/hotloops.sh \
  --qemu   build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64 \
  --plugin build/qemu/contrib/plugins/libhotloops.so \
  --cpu    andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=512 \
  your.elf
```

The report says, for example:

```
measure: --pc-start 0x800001f0 --pc-end 0x80000220  (all of dot_rvv: entry -> ret)
```

```sh
# 2. paste those PCs into hybrid pc mode to get the cycle count on the RTL
andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger pc \
  --pc-start 0x800001f0 --pc-end 0x80000220 \
  --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium your.elf
```

hotloops picked the region (fast, functional QEMU); hybrid pc mode measures that region cycle-accurately. This is exactly why PC mode exists: you never edit the source to add ROI markers - hotloops tells you the addresses.

## Things to get right (from this repo's layout)

- **Override `--qemu` and `--plugin`.** The script auto-resolves them inside the QEMU submodule's own `build/`, but the hybrid_sim build puts them at `build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64` and `build/qemu/contrib/plugins/libhotloops.so`. Pass both explicitly.
- **Match VLEN to your target engine** in `--cpu` (default is `vlen=1024`); otherwise vectorized loops may codegen differently than the engine you measure on.
- **Build the ELF with `-g`** if you want `file:line` and source snippets.
- **RVV filter is on by default.** A scalar hot loop is hidden unless you add `--no-optimize-rvv`.
- The reported `iters` is N-1 per function call (the exit iteration falls through instead of branching back) - expected, not a bug.

message.content: is engine hot plugin?

content.text:
No. hotloops is a QEMU **plugin**, not an engine.

The two are different layers:

- **Engine** = the simulator that runs your program. In `andes-sim` you pick it with `--engine` (QEMU for `fast`, vsim for `cycle`). It produces the cycle/correctness result.
- **Plugin** = a `.so` you load *into* QEMU with `-plugin`. It only observes execution; it does not simulate anything itself.

hotloops is the second kind: `build/qemu/contrib/plugins/libhotloops.so`, loaded into `qemu-system-riscv64`. It watches branches and counts loops. It is a profiling/analysis tool that runs on QEMU.

This repo actually has **two** QEMU plugins, easy to mix up:

| Plugin | File | Job |
|--------|------|-----|
| hotloops | `build/qemu/contrib/plugins/libhotloops.so` | find hot loops -> give you `--pc-start/--pc-end` |
| hybrid handoff | `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so` | drain CPU state at the trigger so vsim can resume |

So the full picture: hotloops (plugin on QEMU) tells you *where* to measure; the hybrid handoff (another plugin on QEMU) does the QEMU->vsim drain; vsim (the cycle **engine**) does the actual measuring.

lastPrompt: I mean the verialtor engines

content.text:
Two different meanings of "plug" - let me separate them, because that is the confusion.

**1. The hotloops plugin does NOT run on the verilator engines.**

hotloops is a QEMU **TCG plugin**. TCG is QEMU's translator. The verilator engines (vsim) are RTL simulators (SystemC + Verilator) - they have no TCG, so there is no place to load a TCG plugin. You cannot profile loops on vsim with hotloops. hotloops only ever runs on QEMU (the `fast` engine).

That is fine for your workflow: you profile on the fast QEMU engine to *find* the hot loop, then measure that loop on the vsim cycle engine. Profiling and measuring are deliberately on different engines.

**2. But the verilator engines ARE "hot-pluggable" - in a totally different sense.**

`andes-sim` discovers engines at runtime. Look at `driver/engine_registry.hpp:1` - the comment calls it "the hot-plug seam." The mechanism:

- The framework has **zero per-engine code**. It only knows the `EngineDescriptor` contract (`driver/engine_descriptor.hpp`).
- At startup `discover_engines()` scans a directory (default `verilator/build`, or `$ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR`) and asks each `sim_*` binary to self-report with `--describe` (or a `<bin>.json` sidecar).
- Each binary returns JSON: its id, kind (`cycle-accurate`), VLEN/DLEN, which triggers it supports, etc.
- Drop a freshly built `sim_ax66_makatau` into the scan dir and it shows up in `andes-sim list engines` with **no andes-sim rebuild**.

So "hot-plug" here means: a new RTL engine plugs into the driver at runtime, like a USB device. It is not a software plugin loaded into a process.

**The naming twist:** internally the type is `verilator`, but the registry rewrites it to `vsim` before you ever see it (`normalize_engine_label`, `engine_registry.hpp:41`). So `--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium` is a hot-plugged Verilator engine.

Summary: verilator engines are hot-**plugged** (drop-in, discovered), but they are not, and cannot run, the hotloops **plugin**.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Author docs/andes_sim_runtime_tutorial.ipynb (empty outputs).

Cells are clean source strings here; nbconvert fills outputs next,
then canon_nb.py canonicalizes to the repo's notebook convention.
"""
import json

def md(text):
    return {"cell_type": "markdown", "metadata": {},
            "source": text.splitlines(keepends=True)}

def code(text):
    return {"cell_type": "code", "execution_count": None, "metadata": {},
            "outputs": [], "source": text.splitlines(keepends=True)}

cells = []

cells.append(md(
"""# andes-sim tutorial: one binary, every engine (the vplat runtime)

A binary linked against a semihosting libgloss (`-lgloss_vh`) can only
do I/O where QEMU intercepts the semihosting trap. vsim has no
semihosting, so that same binary stalls the moment it calls `printf` on
the cycle engine - the old "no syscalls inside the measured region"
rule.

The **vplat runtime** removes that split. It is a small newlib stub
layer (`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`) that talks only to MMIO devices
**both** engines model at the **same** addresses, so ONE ELF runs
unchanged on `fast`, on `cycle`, and across a `hybrid` handoff.

| Channel | Device | Address |
|---------|--------|---------|
| stdout / stderr (fd 0-2) | UART2 16550 | THR `0xf0300020`, LSR `0xf0300034` |
| exit code | SimControl | `0xe0080000` (write a u32 < 256) |
| file io (fd > 2) | HTIF magic-mem | `0xe0080010`, served host-side |

This tutorial builds ONE binary and shows the things you need from a
C program working the same on every engine:

1. compile once, run on `fast` / `cycle` / `hybrid` (stdout, stderr, exit code),
2. an error / trap -> the runtime's trap handler,
3. file io -> the host filesystem via HTIF.
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""import os
from pathlib import Path
root = next(str(d) for d in (Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents)
            if (d / "build" / "andes-sim").exists())
os.chdir(root)
os.environ["PATH"] = f"{root}/build:" + os.environ["PATH"]
print("working dir:", root)
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""## 1. The two flags

The runtime ships prebuilt as `build/runtime/libandes_sim_runtime.a`
(any fixture build makes it, or `./andes-sim build --what runtime`). You
compile with two extra flags - the SAME line for every engine, no
`-mvh`, no `-lgloss_vh`:

    -B build/runtime         # find crt0.o, the linker script, the archive
    -specs=andes-sim.specs   # swap in that startfile + rewrite the lib list

`-specs` swaps the startfile to the runtime's `crt0.o`, adds
`-T andes-sim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and rewrites the library
list to `--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc --end-group`, so no
semihosting can leak into the link. Compiling outside the repo, use the
absolute path to `<repo>/build/runtime` for `-B`.
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""## 2. Compile once, run on three engines

One program, one compile command. It prints to **stdout** and to
**stderr**, runs a trivial loop wrapped in the ROI markers (free HINT
NOPs from `<andes_sim/ROI.h>`, so the binary still runs everywhere), and
returns an exit code.
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
. ./config.env 2>/dev/null      # sets HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"

cat > io_demo.c <<'EOF'
/* One binary for every engine: stdout, stderr, an ROI, an exit code.
 * No semihosting - the two link flags route I/O to MMIO devices both
 * the QEMU (fast) and vsim (cycle) engines model. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <andes_sim/ROI.h>

int main(void)
{
  printf("hello on stdout\\n");            /* fd 1 -> UART */
  fprintf(stderr, "status on stderr\\n");  /* fd 2 -> UART */

  andes_sim_ROI_begin();                  /* free HINT NOPs */
  long sum = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < 1000; i++) sum += i;
  andes_sim_ROI_end();

  printf("sum = %ld\\n", sum);
  return 0;                               /* -> SimControl: process exit 0 */
}
EOF

"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \\
  -B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs io_demo.c -o io_demo.elf

echo "built:"; file io_demo.elf
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""**fast** (QEMU, functional) runs it in well under a second. `andes-sim`
forwards the program's exit code as its own process exit code, so a shell
can branch on it:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
andes-sim run --model fast io_demo.elf </dev/null
echo "process exit: $?"
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""**cycle** runs the WHOLE program on the RTL engine. Same source, same
ELF - only `--model` changed. The stdout/stderr text is byte-identical;
the engine adds its own `[info]` lines and a final cycle total.
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""!andes-sim run --model cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium io_demo.elf
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""**hybrid** fast-forwards on QEMU, then measures the ROI on the RTL. The
markers compiled into the binary above drive `--trigger marker`. stdout
and stderr still print (they run before the window); the final `sum =`
line belongs to the fast leg, so in hybrid the run stops at the exit
marker before printing it.
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""!andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium io_demo.elf
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""## 3. Errors: the trap handler

The runtime installs a machine-mode trap handler (`runtime/trap.S` +
`handler.c`). Any unexpected trap - illegal instruction, bad access -
prints a red `[ERROR]` diagnostic (mcause / mepc / mtval) to stderr and
calls `_exit(mcause)`, which SimControl turns into the process exit
code. This program runs one illegal instruction on purpose:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
. ./config.env 2>/dev/null
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"

cat > trap_demo.c <<'EOF'
#include <stdio.h>
int main(void)
{
  printf("about to run an illegal instruction\\n");
  __asm__ __volatile__(".word 0x00000000");  /* illegal -> trap */
  printf("this line never runs\\n");
  return 0;
}
EOF

"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \\
  -B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs trap_demo.c -o trap_demo.elf
echo "built trap_demo.elf"
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""On **fast**, the handler catches it: `mcause: 0x2` is "illegal
instruction", and the process exits with that code (2), not 0:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
andes-sim run --model fast trap_demo.elf </dev/null
echo "process exit: $?"
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""The **cycle** engine has the same handler and produces the same
diagnostic and the same exit code - the trap path is part of the
portable runtime, not the simulator:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
andes-sim run --model cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium trap_demo.elf </dev/null
echo "process exit: $?"
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""## 4. File io: the host filesystem

For fd > 2 the stubs forward `open`/`read`/`write`/`close`/`fstat` to
the HTIF magic-mem device, which the engine serves on the host. Paths
resolve relative to the **engine process's working directory** (here,
the repo root). This program writes a file and reads it back:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
. ./config.env 2>/dev/null
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"

cat > fileio_demo.c <<'EOF'
#include <stdio.h>
int main(void)
{
  const char *path = "io_demo_file.txt";

  FILE *f = fopen(path, "w");
  if (!f) { printf("fopen(w) failed\\n"); return 1; }
  fprintf(f, "written by the guest, read back by the guest\\n");
  fclose(f);

  char line[80] = {0};
  f = fopen(path, "r");
  if (!f) { printf("fopen(r) failed\\n"); return 1; }
  fgets(line, sizeof line, f);
  fclose(f);

  printf("read back: %s", line);
  return 0;
}
EOF

"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \\
  -B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs fileio_demo.c -o fileio_demo.elf
echo "built fileio_demo.elf"
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""Run on **fast**, then look at the host directory - the guest's file is
really there:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
andes-sim run --model fast fileio_demo.elf </dev/null
echo "--- the host now has the file (engine cwd = $(pwd)) ---"
cat io_demo_file.txt
rm -f io_demo_file.txt
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""The same ELF on **cycle** produces the same file - the QEMU device and
the vsim model serve the HTIF syscall table byte-for-byte:
"""))

cells.append(code(
"""%%bash
andes-sim run --model cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium fileio_demo.elf </dev/null
echo "--- host file after the cycle run ---"
cat io_demo_file.txt
rm -f io_demo_file.txt
"""))

cells.append(md(
"""## Recap

| You want | How |
|----------|-----|
| One portable ELF | compile with `-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs` (no `-lgloss_vh`) |
| Run it three ways | `andes-sim run --model fast\\|cycle\\|hybrid ... your.elf` |
| `printf` / stderr | write to fd 0-2; the runtime drives the UART |
| Exit code | `return n;` (n < 256) -> SimControl -> process exit code |
| Catch a crash | the runtime's trap handler prints `[ERROR]` + exits `mcause` |
| Read/write a file | normal stdio on fd > 2 -> HTIF, served in the engine's cwd |

The ROI markers are free HINT NOPs, so a binary built this way runs
standalone on silicon AND drives `--trigger marker` on hybrid. For a
binary you cannot edit, delimit the region with PC symbols and
`--trigger pc` instead.

More: `docs/andes_sim_demo.ipynb` (model tour),
`docs/andes_sim_gemm_tutorial.ipynb` (cycle measurement),
`docs/USER_GUIDE.md` section 5 (full runtime reference).
"""))

nb = {"cells": cells,
      "metadata": {"kernelspec": {"display_name": "Python 3 (ipykernel)",
                                  "language": "python", "name": "python3"},
                   "language_info": {"name": "python"}},
      "nbformat": 4, "nbformat_minor": 4}

with open("docs/andes_sim_runtime_tutorial.ipynb", "w") as fh:
    json.dump(nb, fh, indent=1)
    fh.write("\n")
print("wrote docs/andes_sim_runtime_tutorial.ipynb with", len(cells), "cells")

# V-scratch reservation: move the transport page out of the program's RAM

## Problem (L26)

The V-register transport stages 32 vector registers through a 4 KB guest-RAM
window at the **compile-time constant** `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` (15 MB).
That address sits *inside* the program's usable RAM, so a program that places
data there (large heap, custom linker script, direct addressing) is silently
corrupted on every resume -- even if it never uses V. Demonstrated by
`tests/fixtures/break_vscratch.S`.

## Core architecture (the fix: scheme D)

Put the scratch page **just above the program's declared RAM**, by making the
physical mmap one page larger than `--mem-size`. The program is told it has
`mem_size`; the simulator quietly maps `mem_size + 4 KB` and parks the scratch
in the extra page. No program layout can reach a page above its own ceiling
without a bug, so the collision class is removed at the root rather than
detected after the fact.

```
            +----------------+ ram_base + mmap_size            (physical top)
V scratch ->|  V scratch 4KB |   mmap_size = mem_size + 4 KB
            +----------------+ ram_base + mem_size             (program ceiling)
            |  program RAM   |   text / data / heap / stack -- all strictly below
            +----------------+ ram_base
```

Scratch GPA = `ram_base + mmap_size - kVScratchBytes` = the **top page of the
mmap**. Both legs already receive `mmap_size`, so the address stays a derived
value with **no new field to keep in sync** -- the only change vs the naive
"top of RAM" is that the mmap is one page bigger than the program's RAM, which
lifts the scratch above everything the program can legally address.

Invariant that must hold at every step: **the host stager and the vsim
Program-Buffer sweep must use the SAME scratch address.** That is why the
"runtime GPA" work (F1) lands as one atomic unit across all three users.

## Features

### F1. Runtime scratch GPA = top page of the mmap span  [state: DONE]
- Verified 2026-06-15: host unit suites green -- v_regfile_xfer 3/3,
  resume_driver 33/33, state_drain 32/32 (incl. new unset-guard tests), +18
  other hybrid suites. vsim builds all 5 CPUs. Full marker e2e 22/22 (incl. V
  fixtures + S/U ax66). `break_vscratch.elf` (the L26 repro) now PASSES under
  `--model hybrid --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium` (was a hang) -- the 0x00FF0000
  sentinel survives because the V transport relocated to the mmap top page.
- Design note: `scratch_gpa` is a required-when-V ctor arg on ResumeDriver /
  StateDrain, defaulting to a `kVScratchGpaUnset` sentinel; a V handoff that
  reaches the sweep unset throws (no silent transport via a bogus address).
  The 60+ non-V unit-test ctor sites pass a stand-in (kScratch); the real glue
  (simulator.hpp `v_scratch_gpa()`) threads the live value through the two
  controllers.
- NOT yet run as e2e: cosim / lockstep V paths (their drain_full /
  drain_checkpoint scratch logic is covered at unit level; same threading).
- Replace the fixed `kVScratchGpa` constant with `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base,
  ram_size) = ram_base + ram_size - kVScratchBytes`. The scratch is the top
  `kVScratchBytes` of whatever RAM span is mapped.
- Host stager (`stage_v_to_scratch` / `read_v_from_scratch`) computes the
  offset as `ram_size - kVScratchBytes` (it already receives the span + base).
- `ResumeDriver` / `StateDrain` take the scratch GPA as a required ctor arg
  (no silent default) and pass it to `pb_v_data_sweep`.
- `simulator.hpp` construction sites compute the GPA from
  `platform.main_memory` and pass it down.
- After F1 alone the scratch is the top page of `mem_size` (scheme A: inside
  program RAM, but far above this runtime's 7 MB stack -- already better than
  the mid-RAM 15 MB constant). F2 lifts it above program RAM (scheme D).
- Key files: `verilator/src/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `resume_driver.hpp`,
  `state_drain.hpp`, `program_buffer.hpp` (caller), `simulator.hpp`,
  `resume_from_qemu.hpp`, `handoff_controller.hpp`, `lockstep_controller.hpp`;
  tests `tests/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.test.cpp`, `resume_driver.test.cpp`,
  `state_drain.test.cpp`.
- Deps: none.

### F2. Map one page above --mem-size; scratch sits above program RAM  [state: DONE]
- Verified 2026-06-16: shared ABI gained `HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`
  (= 32*HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX); v_regfile_xfer's `kVScratchBytes` references it.
  Driver helpers `physical_mmap_bytes()` / `max_program_mem_bytes()` (shm.cpp,
  unit-tested in infra-test); `run_plan.cpp` allocates + reports the physical
  size (program + page); `cmd_run.cpp` caps --mem-size at 2G - page;
  `tests/e2e.sh` mmap split into PROGRAM_SIZE + V_SCRATCH_BYTES.
- Proof: driver builds; 9 driver unit suites + plan-itest pass; V e2e 4/4 with
  the larger mmap. NEW guard `tests/fixtures/break_vscratch_top.S` writes a
  sentinel at the program's LAST page (0x07FFF000 @128M) and PASSES under
  hybrid -- the sentinel survives the V transport, proving the scratch moved to
  the ceiling (0x08000000), above program RAM. Under F1/scheme A that page WAS
  the scratch and the fixture would hang.
- Note: only the hybrid (shared-mmap) path reserves the page; `--model fast`
  (plain `-m`, no handoff, no scratch) is untouched.
- Driver: physical mmap / QEMU backend size / vsim `--shared-mem-size` =
  `mem_size + kVScratchBytes`; the program's RAM ceiling stays `mem_size`.
- 2 GiB edge: `mem_size + 4 KB` would cross into MROM at 0x80000000, so cap
  usable `--mem-size` at `2G - 4 KB` (doc note; 2G was always approximate, L7).
- `tests/e2e.sh` shared-mmap setup must add the page too (it sizes its own
  mmap for the e2e path).
- Key files: `driver/cmd_run.cpp`, `driver/shm.cpp`, `driver/plan.*`,
  `driver/engine_registry.cpp`, `tests/e2e.sh`; driver unit tests.
- Deps: F1.

### F3. Load-time overlap check (loud abort)  [state: DONE]
- Verified 2026-06-16: `elf_load_top()` (elf_syms.cpp) returns the highest
  PT_LOAD `p_paddr + p_memsz`; `cmd_run.cpp` rejects a hybrid run when that
  exceeds the scratch GPA (ram_base + --mem-size). Unit: elf-syms test
  (load-top on a fixture + non-ELF err) + 9/9 driver suites. Integration:
  `--mem-size 1M` on a fixture linked at 0x100000 aborts with "ELF static image
  ends at 0x100036, overlapping the reserved V-transport scratch page at
  0x100000 ... raise --mem-size"; default 128M runs clean (no false positive).
- Scope: static image only (PT_LOAD). Runtime heap/stack growth into the
  scratch is already impossible under F2 (scratch is above the program ceiling).
- Reject any ELF segment (and ideally the initial SP) overlapping
  `[scratch_gpa, scratch_gpa + kVScratchBytes)`. With F2 this never fires for
  well-behaved programs; it converts the paranoid "program pokes past its own
  ceiling" case from silent corruption into a clear error.
- Key files: driver ELF loader / vsim `state_loader.hpp`; new unit test.
- Deps: F1, F2.
